entities/disfuncion-parasimpatico/descri.text: Dysfunction of the parasympathetic autonomic nervous system. Anatomically, the nervous system is divided into two parts: the central nervous system (CNS), which is in the head, and the peripheral nervous system (PNS), which extends from the spinal column to the rest of the body. Functionally, the nervous system is divided into two parts: the somatic nervous system (SNS) and the autonomic nervous system (ANS). The central nervous system (CNS) is formed by the encephalon and the spinal cord. The encephalon is the part of the CNS that is protected by the bones of the skull; it is formed by the cerebrum, the cerebellum and the brainstem. The cerebrum is the most voluminous part; it is divided into two hemispheres, a right one and a left one, separated by the interhemispheric fissure and connected by the corpus callosum. The cerebellum is in the lower and posterior part of the encephalon, next to the brainstem. The brainstem is composed of the midbrain, the pons and the medulla oblongata. It connects the brain with the spinal cord. The spinal cord is an extension of the encephalon, like a cord that extends through the inside of the spinal column. The peripheral nervous system (PNS) is formed by the cranial nerves and the spinal nerves. Both emerge from the CNS and run throughout the body. The cranial nerves are 12 pairs that send sensory information from the neck and head to the CNS; likewise, they receive motor commands from the CNS for control of the skeletal musculature of the neck and head. The spinal nerves are 31 pairs that are responsible for sending sensory information from the trunk and limbs to the CNS; likewise, they receive motor commands from the CNS for control of the skeletal musculature of the trunk and limbs, and these commands are conducted through the spinal cord. The somatic nervous system (SNS), also called the nervous system of relational life, is formed by the set of neurons that regulate voluntary or conscious functions in the body, for example, muscle movement. The autonomic nervous system (ANS), also called the vegetative nervous system or visceral nervous system, is formed by the set of neurons that regulate involuntary or unconscious functions in the body, for example, intestinal movement. In turn, the ANS is classified into sympathetic (thoracic and lumbar region of the spine --> center) and parasympathetic (cervical and sacral region of the spine --> ends), systems whose functions are mostly antagonistic. The sympathetic nervous system prepares us for action. This is the system that mediates the hormonal stress response. Fight-or-flight behaviors are mediated by the sympathetic system. It increases the heart rate and dilates the bronchi and the pupils. It stimulates the adrenal glands. Excessive sweating, or hyperhidrosis, of the hands, armpits or face is related to overstimulation of the sympathetic system. The sympathetic nervous system is responsible for regulating the homeostatic mechanisms (the ability to maintain a stable internal condition by compensating for changes in the environment) of living organisms. The fibers of this system reach almost all the organs and systems of the body, from the pupil of the eye to the control of intestinal motility. The sympathetic system helps us feel sensations of cold or heat. Some of the actions of the sympathetic nervous system are the following: it dilates the pupil of the eye, reduces saliva production, dilates the bronchi in the lungs, increases the heart rate, constricts the blood vessels, stimulates the sweat glands, decreases urine secretion in the kidneys, promotes ejaculation, and inhibits the involuntary contraction movements of the stomach. The parasympathetic nervous system is responsible for regulating the internal organs during rest and digestion and the activities that occur when the body is at rest, such as sleep. Some of the actions of the parasympathetic nervous system are the following: it constricts the pupil of the eye, increases saliva production, constricts the bronchi in the lungs, decreases the heart rate, increases the movements and contractions of the stomach, lowers blood pressure, increases urine secretion in the kidneys, increases fuel storage, increases our resistance to infections, increases the circulation of oxygen to non-vital organs if necessary, provides fuel and eliminates waste from the skin, digestive tract and reproductive organs. The work of the parasympathetic system complements that of the sympathetic system. Both systems work in natural opposition.

entities/disfuncion-paratiroides/descrip.text: Parathyroid gland dysfunction. Blood calcium and phosphorus levels are altered. Hypocalcemia syndrome (low blood calcium levels). Osteoporosis: a product of hypercalcemia (increased concentration of calcium in the blood, that is, it does not bind to bone). It can produce tetany, which consists of spasms of the striated musculature (painful contractions of the muscles of the limbs). The parathyroid glands are endocrine glands located in the neck, behind the thyroid lobes. They produce parathyroid hormone, or parathormone (PTH). There are usually four parathyroid glands, two superior and two inferior, but occasionally there may be five or more. Parathyroid hormone is involved in the regulation of calcium and phosphorus metabolism. Parathormone produces hypercalcemia (increased concentration of calcium in the blood) if its secretion increases; on the other hand, its deficiency produces hypocalcemia (low levels of calcium in the blood) and, as a consequence, can induce tetany, which consists of spasms of the striated musculature (painful contractions of the muscles of the limbs). In addition, it regulates the concentration of calcium ions in the extracellular fluid, increasing bone resorption by stimulating osteoclasts to break down bone, which releases more calcium into the bloodstream. In the case of calcium ions, what it does is increase the proximal resorption of these ions, mainly from bone, in order to raise blood calcium levels. It therefore has an effect opposite to that of calcitonin. Likewise, it regulates the levels of phosphorus ions in the blood, lowering their concentration in this medium by increasing their renal excretion (hyperphosphaturia).

entities/disfuncion-parotida/description.text: Dysfunction in the production of insulin, thyroxine and calcitonin. Improves appetite. Parotid dysfunction causes a drop in hormones. The parotids have a direct influence on the hormone production of three other glands: parathyroid, thyroid and pancreas. As soon as food is tasted, the parotids stimulate the production of thyroxine, calcitonin and insulin to complement the subsequent digestion of the food. It is associated with bone disorders due to decalcification (lack of calcitonin), and with body weight and digestive disorders.

entities/disfuncion-peritoneo/descriptio.text: Peritoneal dysfunction. The peritoneum is the membrane that covers most of the organs of the abdomen. It is composed of a layer of mesothelium resting on a thin layer of connective tissue. The peritoneum is structured in two layers: the outer layer, called the parietal peritoneum, is attached to the abdominal wall, and the inner layer, the visceral peritoneum, envelops the organs located within the abdominal cavity. The space between the two layers is called the peritoneal cavity; it contains a small amount of lubricating fluid (about 50 ml) that allows the two layers to slide over each other. Most of the abdominal organs are attached to the abdominal wall by the mesentery, a part of the peritoneum through which the organs are supplied by blood vessels, lymphatics and nerves.

entities/disfuncion-piloro/description.text: The pylorus controls the passage of food into the intestine. The pylorus is the lower valve that connects the stomach to the duodenum. The pylorus constitutes a small portion of the stomach that serves as the gateway to the duodenum (the beginning of the small intestine), closing or opening to prevent or allow the passage of food. This function allows food to be digested by the stomach by preventing food from passing prematurely into the intestine under the effect of gravity. When the process of gastric digestion has finished, the pylorus opens, letting the chyme (a dense fluid formed by the food bolus and the gastric juices) pass into the intestine, where a different type of digestion takes place.

entities/disfuncion-pineal/description.text: Dysfunction of the pineal gland. Vitiligo appears as a result of pineal gland dysfunction + liver dysfunction + an emotional problem. It is a degenerative skin disease in which the melanocytes (the cells responsible for skin pigmentation) die, so that melanin (the substance that produces skin pigmentation) stops being produced in the area where cell death has occurred. The pineal gland acts on pigmentation, sexuality and the adrenal glands. Its dysfunction affects the production of corticosteroids, which are a variety of hormones of the steroid group (produced by the cortex of the adrenal glands) and their derivatives. Corticosteroids are involved in a variety of physiological mechanisms, including those that regulate inflammation, the immune system, carbohydrate metabolism, protein catabolism and plasma electrolyte levels and, finally, those that characterize the response to stress. The pineal gland, also known as the pineal body, conarium or epiphysis cerebri, is a small endocrine gland (it secretes hormones) in the brain of vertebrates. It produces melatonin, a hormone derived from serotonin that affects the modulation of sleep patterns, both circadian and seasonal rhythms. Its shape resembles a small pine cone (hence its name), and it is located in the epithalamus near the center of the brain, between the two hemispheres, tucked into a groove where the two halves of the thalamus join. The pineal gland is responsible for producing melatonin. This pair normalizes the generation of melatonin. In Homo sapiens there is a constant synthesis of melatonin that decreases abruptly around 30 years of age; from adolescence onward, calcifications called corpora arenacea usually form in the gland. It has been observed that the functions of melatonin include, among others, regulating the biological clock and reducing oxidation. Melatonin deficits may be accompanied by insomnia and depression and could cause a gradual acceleration of aging. Melatonin is the most potent endogenous antioxidant known. Its functions are the following: 1) Its primary function is to coordinate and regulate biological rhythms (hunger, sleep, etc.) 2) It harmonizes the autonomic system with the environment. 3) It controls the functioning of the body's neuroendocrine centers. 4) It combats jet lag. 5) It regulates body temperature. 6) It regulates sleep, helps you sleep better and allows you to wake up more rested. 7) It participates in a wide variety of cellular and neurophysiological processes. 8) It prevents premature calcification in childhood, favoring bone growth. 9) It controls the onset of puberty. 10) It protects the central nervous system 11) It enhances and stimulates the immune system. 12) It helps prevent and treat diseases, including cancer. 13) It promotes the function of other glands. 14) It calms tension and stress and relaxes the muscles, promoting drowsiness. 15) It improves mood and the sense of well-being. 16) It causes apoptosis (programmed cell destruction or death brought about by the organism itself) of cancer cells in the thymus. Some diseases that can be prevented or treated with adequate generation of melatonin are the following: diseases of aging (Parkinson's, Alzheimer's), neurodegenerative diseases, cardiovascular diseases, headaches, erectile dysfunction, depression, macular degeneration, edema, ulcerative colitis, cephalalgia, asthma, sleep disturbances, anxiety, arteriosclerosis, rheumatoid arthritis, cancer, tiredness, cataracts, cystitis, respiratory insufficiency, arrhythmias, gastroesophageal reflux, burns, tuberculosis, circadian rhythm disorders (cyclical physical and mental changes (24 hours)), memory problems, high blood pressure, infections, maculopathies, skin lesions, migraine, tachycardia, aluminum or lead toxicity, wounds, intestinal disorders, osteoarthritis, pancreatitis, hyperpigmentation, hypertension, glaucoma.

entities/disfuncion-prostata/description.text: Prostate dysfunction. Helps sphincter control. The prostate is a chestnut-shaped glandular organ of the male reproductive system in the great majority of mammals, located in front of the rectum, below and at the outlet of the urinary bladder, although it may be attached to it. The prostate functions as a secondary bladder that exerts pressure so that semen is expelled from the urethra to the outside; it is also able to close off the bladder outlet to prevent it from releasing its contents during intercourse. The prostate is connected to the testicles by the vasa deferentia, which ascend to a level higher than the bladder, which prevents urine from contaminating the scrotum. The prostate gland contributes: antigen, fibrinogen, spermine, zinc (Zn, with bactericidal properties), magnesium (Mg, gives semen its milky appearance) and enzymes. Just above and to the sides of the prostate gland are the seminal vesicles, which produce most of the seminal fluid. The prostate surrounds the first part of the urethra, the duct through which urine and semen travel to the penis. Male hormones stimulate the prostate gland from fetal development onward. The prostate continues to grow until adulthood is reached and maintains its size as long as male hormones are produced. If male hormones disappear, the prostate gland cannot develop and shrinks, sometimes almost to the point of disappearing.

entities/disfuncion-sexual/description.text: Substantial alterations of libido. It also controls excessive sexuality --> It normalizes. Sexual dysfunction is the term for difficulty during any stage of the sexual act (which includes desire, arousal, orgasm and resolution) that prevents the individual or couple from enjoying sexual activity. Sexual dysfunctions may manifest at the beginning of a person's sexual life or may develop later. Some may develop gradually over time, and others may appear suddenly as a total or partial inability to participate in one or more stages of the sexual act. The causes of sexual dysfunctions may be physical, psychological or both. The Cervical spine-Sacrum pair helps the testicles descend.

entities/disfuncion-simpatico/descriptio.text: Dysfunction of the parasympathetic autonomic nervous system. Anatomically, the nervous system is divided into two parts: the central nervous system (CNS), which is in the head, and the peripheral nervous system (PNS), which extends from the spinal column to the rest of the body. Functionally, the nervous system is divided into two parts: the somatic nervous system (SNS) and the autonomic nervous system (ANS). The central nervous system (CNS) is formed by the encephalon and the spinal cord. The encephalon is the part of the CNS that is protected by the bones of the skull; it is formed by the cerebrum, the cerebellum and the brainstem. The cerebrum is the most voluminous part; it is divided into two hemispheres, a right one and a left one, separated by the interhemispheric fissure and connected by the corpus callosum. The cerebellum is in the lower and posterior part of the encephalon, next to the brainstem. The brainstem is composed of the midbrain, the pons and the medulla oblongata. It connects the brain with the spinal cord. The spinal cord is an extension of the encephalon, like a cord that extends through the inside of the spinal column. The cranial nerves are 12 pairs that send sensory information from the neck and head to the CNS; likewise, they receive motor commands from the CNS for control of the skeletal musculature of the neck and head. The spinal nerves are 31 pairs that are responsible for sending sensory information from the trunk and limbs to the CNS; likewise, they receive motor commands from the CNS for control of the skeletal musculature of the trunk and limbs, and these commands are conducted through the spinal cord. The somatic nervous system (SNS), also called the nervous system of relational life, is formed by the set of neurons that regulate voluntary or conscious functions in the body, for example, muscle movement. The autonomic nervous system (ANS), also called the vegetative nervous system or visceral nervous system, is formed by the set of neurons that regulate involuntary or unconscious functions in the body, for example, intestinal movement. In turn, the ANS is classified into sympathetic (thoracic and lumbar region of the spine --> center) and parasympathetic (cervical and sacral region of the spine --> ends), systems whose functions are mostly antagonistic. The sympathetic nervous system prepares us for action. This is the system that mediates the hormonal stress response. Fight-or-flight behaviors are mediated by the sympathetic system. It increases the heart rate and dilates the bronchi and the pupils. It stimulates the adrenal glands. Excessive sweating, or hyperhidrosis, of the hands, armpits or face is related to overstimulation of the sympathetic system. The sympathetic nervous system is responsible for regulating the homeostatic mechanisms (the ability to maintain a stable internal condition by compensating for changes in the environment) of living organisms. The fibers of this system reach almost all the organs and systems of the body, from the pupil of the eye to the control of intestinal motility. The sympathetic system helps us feel sensations of cold or heat. Some of the actions of the sympathetic nervous system are the following: it dilates the pupil of the eye, reduces saliva production, dilates the bronchi in the lungs, increases the heart rate, constricts the blood vessels, stimulates the sweat glands, decreases urine secretion in the kidneys, promotes ejaculation, and inhibits the involuntary contraction movements of the stomach. The parasympathetic nervous system is responsible for regulating the internal organs during rest and digestion and the activities that occur when the body is at rest, such as sleep. Some of the actions of the parasympathetic nervous system are the following: it constricts the pupil of the eye, increases saliva production, constricts the bronchi in the lungs, decreases the heart rate, increases the movements and contractions of the stomach, lowers blood pressure, increases urine secretion in the kidneys, increases fuel storage, increases our resistance to infections, increases the circulation of oxygen to non-vital organs if necessary, provides fuel and eliminates waste from the skin, digestive tract and reproductive organs. The work of the parasympathetic system complements that of the sympathetic system. Both systems work in natural opposition.

entities/disfuncion-suprarrenales/descri.text: The adrenal glands are two retroperitoneal structures, the right one triangular in shape and the left one semilunar, both located above the kidneys. Their function is to regulate stress responses through the synthesis of corticosteroids (mainly cortisol) and catecholamines (above all adrenaline). Their dysfunction can lead to Addison's disease with generalized edema, chronic fatigue, and inability to respond to inflammation. Addison's disease is a hormone deficiency caused by damage to the adrenal glands, resulting in primary adrenocortical hypofunction or insufficiency. Addison's original description of this disease is: languor and general weakness, hypokinetic activity of the heart, gastric irritability and a peculiar change in skin coloration.

entities/disfuncion-testiculos/descripti.text: Testicular dysfunction. Lack of testosterone production. The testicles are the male gonads, co-producers of spermatozoa and sex hormones (testosterone). They are the glandular organs that form the most important part of the male reproductive system.

entities/disfuncion-timo/description.text: Thymus dysfunction. It governs the production of T lymphocytes of the immune system. When it fails, immunodeficiency results. The thymus is a specialized organ of the immune system. Within the thymus gland, T cells or T lymphocytes mature. T cells are critical for the adaptive immune system, in which the body adapts specifically to external invaders.

entities/disfuncion-tiroides/description.text: Thyroid gland dysfunction. Thyroid hormone is directly related to weight. It can produce goiter, which is the enlargement of the thyroid gland. Externally it appears as a mass in the anterior-inferior part of the neck just below the larynx. Hand tremor. Fluid retention. It can produce lymphomas when associated with a bacterium. The thyroid gland regulates the body's metabolism, produces proteins and regulates the body's sensitivity to other hormones. It is a neuroendocrine gland located just below the Adam's apple, next to the thyroid cartilage over the trachea. This gland regulates the production of calcitonin. Calcitonin is a linear peptide hormone composed of 32 amino acids that is involved in regulating calcium and phosphorus metabolism. This hormone is produced in the parafollicular cells (also called C cells) of the thyroid gland, and its function consists of reducing blood calcium levels (Ca2+), opposing the action of parathyroid hormone (parathormone). Specifically, it affects blood calcium levels in four ways: 1) It inhibits intestinal absorption of Ca2+ (reducing calcemia, or the concentration of calcium in the blood). 2) It inhibits bone resorption (loss) (again reducing calcemia). 3) It inhibits phosphate reabsorption in the renal tubules (reducing its concentration in the blood). 4) It increases the excretion of Ca2+ and Mg2+ by the kidneys.

entities/disfuncion-vejiga-urinaria/desc.text: Urinary bladder dysfunction. The urinary bladder is a hollow musculomembranous organ that forms part of the urinary tract and that receives urine from the ureters, stores it and expels it through the urethra to the outside of the body during urination. The ureter is a tube-shaped retroperitoneal urinary passage that carries urine from the kidney to the urinary bladder, and whose inner mucosal lining is of mesodermal origin. The urethra is the duct through which urine passes in the final phase of the urinary process, from the urinary bladder to the outside of the body during urination. The function of the urethra is excretory in both sexes, and it also fulfills a reproductive function in men by allowing the passage of semen from the seminal vesicles, which open into the prostate, to the outside; that is, this duct is shared by the urinary and reproductive systems.

entities/disfuncion-vesicula-biliar/desc.text: The gallbladder is an organ that forms part of the digestive system of humans and quadruped animals (except horses and deer). It is located below the liver. It is a small, hollow, ovoid or pear-shaped viscus, approximately 5 to 7 cm in its greatest diameter. It connects with the small intestine (duodenum) through the common bile duct, or choledochus. The function of the gallbladder is to store and concentrate the bile secreted by the liver, which reaches the gallbladder through the hepatic and cystic ducts, until it is required by the digestive process. It holds a volume of about 50 ml of bile, which it releases into the duodenum. It stores the biliary secretion until an appropriate stimulus causes its release through contraction of its muscular wall. Secretion of bile by the gallbladder is stimulated by food intake, especially when it contains meat or fat; at that moment it contracts and expels the concentrated bile into the duodenum. Bile is a greenish-brown fluid whose function is to emulsify fats, producing microspheres and thus facilitating their digestion and absorption, in addition to promoting intestinal movements, thereby preventing putrefaction. Situations that delay or obstruct the flow of bile cause gallbladder diseases. Excess cholesterol and waste products of hemoglobin metabolism, such as bilirubin, as well as some medications, are also excreted through the bile.

entities/dislexia/description.text: Dyslexia is difficulty learning to read fluently despite the children being intelligent girls and boys with normal motivation and schooling. Reading is very hard for them; it is slow, and they make frequent errors such as omissions of letters or syllables, substitutions, inversions (changing the order of letters or syllables), additions, joining and fragmenting of words, corrections, hesitations and skipping lines while reading. As a result, their comprehension of what they read is also poor. It is the most frequent specific learning disorder among schoolchildren. It is often a cause of school failure and has repercussions on the emotional development of the child and of the whole family. It is difficulty learning to read fluently despite the children being intelligent girls and boys with normal motivation and schooling. Its cause is unclear; it is probably a process of neurobiological nature with a genetic basis. Dyslexia is based on a phonological deficit. That is, a difficulty in correctly associating each written letter with its corresponding sound. It is often associated with other problems such as: attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, dysgraphia (defective writing without any significant neurological or intellectual disorder), dysorthographia (writing errors that affect the word rather than its tracing or handwriting), dyscalculia (innate difficulty in processing numbers, arithmetic calculation and problem solving), developmental coordination disorder (clumsiness, poor coordination and a tendency to fall).

entities/dismenorrea/description.text: Dysmenorrhea or painful menstruation is an irregularity of menstrual function characterized by painful periods that appear with menstruation. Some symptoms may be the following: leg cramps, intense pelvic or abdominal pain, lower back pain (at kidney level), headache, nausea, dizziness, vomiting, excessive sweating, fainting, fatigue, as well as anxiety, irritability or depression.

entities/disnea/description.text: Dyspnea is a breathing difficulty usually experienced as shortness of breath. It results in a subjective feeling of discomfort that frequently originates in deficient breathing. This experience arises from interactions involving multiple physiological, psychological, social and environmental factors, which in turn may induce anything from physiological responses to secondary behaviors. Some of the causes of dyspnea are the following: heart disease, clots in the arteries of the lungs (pulmonary embolism), bronchiolitis, pneumonia, pulmonary hypertension, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), asthma and other chronic lung problems.

entities/dispepsia/description.text: The term dyspepsia encompasses any disorder of gastric secretion, gastrointestinal motility or gastric sensitivity that disturbs digestion, and designates any functional alteration associated with the digestive system. It generally occurs when there is no healthy diet. Its origin may lie in a physical or emotional disorder, and it is characterized by digestive disturbances resulting from gastric and intestinal dysfunctions. It produces physical discomfort of the upper gastrointestinal tract associated with the ingestion of solid or liquid food. It presents symptoms such as burning or acidity, belching, gaseous distension, flatulence, a feeling of fullness or abdominal pressure, nausea and vomiting.

entities/displacia-celular/description.text: Cellular dysplasia is an abnormality in the appearance of cells due to alterations in their maturation process. It is a cellular lesion characterized by an irreversible modification of DNA that causes alteration of cell morphology and/or function. If an increase in the number of cells occurs, it becomes hyperplasia. Dysplasia can also eventually lead to a neoplasm. Dysplastic cells undergo proliferation and atypical alterations that affect their size, shape and organization. This may indicate that they are at an early stage of evolution toward transformation into a neoplasm. Therefore, dysplasia is a preneoplastic or precancerous change.

entities/displacia-cervical/description.text: Cervical dysplasia refers to abnormal changes in the cells on the surface of the cervix. This is the lower part of the uterus (womb) that opens into the upper part of the vagina. These changes are not cancer, but they can lead to cervical cancer if not treated. Cervical dysplasia can occur at any age, but it is almost always seen in women aged 25 to 35. Very often, cervical dysplasia is caused by the human papillomavirus (HPV), a common virus that spreads through sexual contact. There are many types of HPV. Some types lead to cervical cancer or cervical dysplasia. Other types of HPV can cause genital warts. Factors that can increase the risk of cervical dysplasia are the following: having sexual intercourse before the age of 18, having a baby before the age of 16, having multiple sexual partners, having other diseases or using medications that suppress the immune system, smoking.

entities/distension-abdominal/descriptio.text: Abdominal distension is a condition in which the abdomen (belly) feels full and tight. The abdomen may look swollen (distended). Some of the causes of abdominal distension are: swallowing air (a nervous habit), constipation, gastroesophageal reflux, irritable bowel syndrome, lactose and other food intolerances, overeating, bacterial overgrowth in the small intestine, weight gain.

entities/diverticulos/description.text: A diverticulum is an outpouching of the intestinal wall. It can also be defined as an abnormal sac or pouch protruding from the wall of a hollow organ such as the colon. Patients usually present clinical pictures with pain in the left iliac fossa, fever and an increased white blood cell concentration in the blood. They may also present diarrhea, nausea and rectal bleeding.

entities/dolor-abdominal/description.text: The abdomen is a cavity of the human body located between the lower surface of the thorax and the upper surface of the pelvis and the lower limbs, in mammals separated from the rib cage by the diaphragm. Almost all the viscera contained in the abdominal cavity belong to the digestive system and are located in the front two-thirds of the abdomen. Other organs, such as the kidney, the adrenal gland and the female genital system, are intra-abdominal. The posterior third of the abdomen comprises the lumbar vertebrae, the sacrococcygeal bone and the iliac bones. Abdominal pain can come from any of the organs housed in the abdominal cavity. Severe pain does not always indicate a serious problem, and mild pain does not necessarily mean that it is a minor problem.

entities/dolor-articular/description.text: Joint pain. The following biomagnetic pairs relieve pain arising in any joint of the body; they must be placed simultaneously. 1) Pituitary gland - Bladder 2) Radius - Radius 3) Thyroid gland - Medulla oblongata 4) Bladder - Pituitary gland. A joint is the junction between two or more bones, a bone and cartilage, or a bone and the teeth. The branch of anatomy responsible for the study of joints is arthrology. The most important functions of joints are to constitute points of union between the components of the skeleton (bones, cartilage and teeth) and to facilitate mechanical movements (in the case of movable joints), giving the body elasticity and plasticity, to allow growth of the brain, as well as being sites of growth (in the case of the epiphyseal plates).

entities/dolor-de-brazos/description.text: Pain is an unpleasant sensory (physical) experience that can be felt by all living beings that have a central nervous system. It is a feedback mechanism that signals to the organism everything that harms it. It is thanks to pain that every organism learns to take care of itself, which results in a prolongation of life. It should not be confused with suffering, which originates in the psychological or emotional sphere and always occurs consciously. Pain, as a defense mechanism, is necessary to prolong the life of the physical body. Suffering, as an emotional response, is an indicator of a lack of maturity in the person who experiences it. Arm pain occurs along the bone called the humerus, which at its upper end articulates with the scapula and at its lower end with the radius and ulna.

entities/dolor-de-cabeza/contagion.text: The most common types of headache are probably caused by muscle tension in the shoulders, neck, scalp and jaw. This type of headache is called tension headache. It may be related to stress, depression, anxiety, head trauma, or holding the head and neck in an abnormal position. Migraines can be triggered by foods such as chocolate, certain cheeses or monosodium glutamate (MSG). Caffeine withdrawal, lack of sleep and alcohol can also trigger them.

entities/dolor-de-cabeza/description.text: A migraine or headache involves severe pain that generally occurs with other symptoms, such as changes in vision, sensitivity to noise or light, or nausea. With a migraine the pain may be throbbing, pounding or pulsating; it tends to start on one side of the head and can spread to both sides; the pain generally worsens as one tries to move from one place to another.

entities/dolor-de-cintura/description.text: The waist is a part of the abdomen located between the thorax and the hip. In people with proportionate measurements, the waist is the narrowest part of the trunk. Pain felt at the waist or indicative of a problem originating there. The pain is characterized as mild, stabbing or lancinating, or as a burning sensation. It may be confused with rheumatism. The quadriceps femoris is the most powerful and voluminous muscle in the entire human body. It is the one that bears our weight and allows us to walk, stroll, sit and run. It is called the quadriceps because it has four muscle heads.

entities/dolor-de-codo/description.text: Elbow pain can be caused by many problems. A common cause in adults is tendinitis. This is inflammation and injury of the tendons, which are the soft tissues that attach muscle to bone. People who play racquet sports are more likely to injure the tendons on the outside of the elbow. This condition is commonly called tennis elbow. Golfers are more likely to injure the tendons on the inside of the elbow. Gardening, playing baseball, using a screwdriver or overusing the wrist and arm are other common causes of elbow tendinitis. Young children frequently develop "nursemaid's elbow", usually when someone pulls them by the outstretched arm. The bones stretch and separate momentarily, and a ligament slips between them. The ligament becomes trapped when the bones try to snap back into place. Children will usually silently refuse to use the arm, but often cry out at any attempt to bend or straighten the elbow. This condition is also called elbow subluxation (a partial dislocation).

entities/dolor-de-cuello/contagion.text: Neck pain can be caused by a problem related to stress or to trauma (a blow). If the pain is due to stress, the pairs for that condition must be applied.

entities/dolor-de-espalda/description.text: Back pain is pain felt in the back or arising from a problem originating there. The pain is characterized as dull, stabbing or lancinating, or as a burning sensation. The pain can radiate to the arms, hands, legs and feet, and can include a sensation of paresthesia (tingling, numbness or deadness) or weakness or loss of sensation in the legs and arms. The anatomical classification follows the segments of the spine: neck (cervical) pain, mid-back pain or central lumbago, low back pain and coccyx pain, with the most common pain being found in the lumbar vertebrae. The pain can originate from the muscles, nerves, bones, joints or other structures of the spinal column. Internal structures such as the gallbladder and the pancreas can also cause referred pain in the back.

entities/dolor-de-estomago/description.text: Pain is an unpleasant sensory (physical) experience that can be felt by all living beings that have a central nervous system. It should not be confused with suffering, which originates in the psychological or emotional sphere and always occurs consciously. Pain, as a defense mechanism, is necessary to prolong the life of the physical body. Suffering, as an emotional response, is an indicator of a lack of maturity in the person who experiences it. Stomach ache may involve one or more of the following organs: final part of the esophagus, stomach, small intestine, large intestine, liver, gallbladder, pancreas, appendix, kidneys, spleen.

entities/dolor-de-garganta/contagion.text: The most frequent causes of odynophagia are throat infections such as tonsillitis or pharyngitis, infections by the bacterium Streptococcus or the fungus Candida, herpes or cytomegalovirus, and also the ingestion of caustic substances or aggressive medications. In addition, dental conditions such as pericoronitis, stomatitis and third-molar surgery may be found as causes.

entities/dolor-de-garganta/description.text: Odynophagia is the medical term describing the symptom consisting of a sore throat produced on swallowing fluids, frequently as a consequence of inflammation of the esophageal mucosa or the esophageal muscles. The intensity of the pain can range from mild to so severe that patients cannot even swallow their own saliva. Depending on its intensity, it can produce dysphagia.

entities/dolor-de-hombro/description.text: Pain is an unpleasant sensory (physical) experience that can be felt by all living beings that have a central nervous system. Pain, as a defense mechanism, is necessary to prolong the life of the physical body. Suffering, as an emotional response, is an indicator of a lack of maturity in the person who experiences it. Shoulder pain occurs along the bone called the clavicle, which joins the arm to the trunk of the body.

entities/dolor-de-rodillas/description.text: Knee pain occurs along the joint of the same name, in the lower limbs. Some of its causes are: overweight, overuse of the knee, arthritis and others. Pain, as a defense mechanism, is necessary to prolong the life of the physical body. Suffering, as an emotional response, is an indication of a lack of maturity in the person who experiences it. Sacral pain occurs along the bone of the same name located at the waist.

entities/dolor-de-tobillo/description.text: Ankle pain occurs along the joint of the same name, where the leg joins the foot. Pain is an unpleasant sensory (physical) experience that can be felt by all living beings that have a central nervous system. It is a feedback mechanism that signals to the organism everything that harms it. It is thanks to pain that every organism learns to take care of itself, which results in a prolongation of life. It should not be confused with suffering, which originates in the psychological or emotional sphere and always occurs consciously. Pain, as a defense mechanism, is necessary to prolong the life of the physical body. Suffering, as an emotional response, is an indicator of a lack of maturity in the person who experiences it.

entities/dolor-emocional/description.text: Emotional pain is the negative feeling that arises in certain situations or problems, generally related to a loss or to a problem that affects us significantly. It arises at the moment we are hurt physically or emotionally. It is a single emotion, its duration is relatively short, and it is proportional to the event that produced it. It can be any emotion that affects us: sadness over a loss, stress at the need to face a problem, anger, frustration, etc. Suffering goes one step further. Suffering is the cognitive-emotional response we have to physical pain or to a painful situation. It is a set of intertwined emotions and thoughts, acquiring much more intensity and duration than emotional pain. In fact, suffering can last indefinitely, even though the situation that caused it has already been resolved.

entities/dolor-facial/description.text: Facial pain can be dull and throbbing or an intense, stabbing discomfort in the face or forehead. It can occur on one or both sides. Pain that begins in the face can be caused by a nerve disorder, an injury or an infection. This type of pain can also start elsewhere in the body.

entities/dolor-muscular/description.text: Muscle pains or myalgias consist of pains or discomfort that may affect one or several muscles of the body. Ligaments, tendons and fasciae may also be involved. The causes are very varied. The main ones include overuse, strain or muscle injuries from intense exercise or physical work. Likewise, muscle pain can be a symptom of certain diseases that affect the whole body, notably fibromyalgia.

entities/dolor-toracico/description.text: Chest pain is discomfort or pain felt at some point along the front of the body between the neck and the upper abdomen. Many people who experience chest pain fear a heart attack; however, there are many possible causes. Some causes are not dangerous to health, while others are serious and in some cases potentially fatal. Any organ or tissue in the chest can be the source of the pain, including the heart, lungs, esophagus, muscles, ribs, tendons or nerves. Pain can also spread to the chest from the neck, abdomen and back.

entities/dolores-dorso-lumbar/descriptio.text: Low back pain is pain localized in the area between the lower rib cage and the sacral region, which sometimes may involve the gluteal region. Several factors make the lumbosacral region much more vulnerable than other regions of the body to the various destabilizing forces involved in maintaining the upright position. These destabilizing forces have a single origin: the force of gravity. This disorder is very common in people with a sedentary lifestyle, especially those who work seated.

entities/duda/description.text: Doubt can extend to the fields of decision and action, or affect only belief, faith or the validity of a piece of knowledge. If it is preceded by a conventionally accepted "truth", doubt implies insecurity about its validity.

entities/ebola/contagion.text: The virus can be contracted through contact with the blood or body fluids of infected animals (usually monkeys or fruit bats). Once a human being is infected, the disease can also spread from person to person.

entities/ebola/description.text: Ebola virus disease or Ebola hemorrhagic fever, also known as Ebola disease or simply Ebola, is a disease caused in humans by the Ebola virus. Symptoms normally begin between two days and three weeks after contracting the virus, with fever, sore throat, muscle pain and headache. These are generally followed by nausea, vomiting and diarrhea, together with liver and kidney failure. At that point, some patients begin to suffer hemorrhagic complications.

entities/echinococcus-granulosus/descrip.text: Echinococcus granulosus is a species of flatworm of the class Cestoda that, in its adult form, is a parasite of the small intestine of the dog (and occasionally other canids), while in its larval stage it parasitizes sheep or goats (and occasionally other herbivores); secondarily or accidentally it can also parasitize other animals, including cattle, horses, pigs, some rodents, deer, elk, marsupials, primates and humans, producing hydatidosis or hydatid cyst. Hydatidosis, echinococcosis or hydatid cyst is a disease caused by larvae of Echinococcus granulosus, which are often ingested in accidentally contaminated food. Hydatidosis is detected by the occurrence of anaphylactic shock. Its incidence is very low, and hydatid cysts generally remain asymptomatic for years. The hydatid or cyst follows a slow "tumor-like" growth pattern, evolving over years. When it is located in the liver and obstructs the bile ducts, it causes alteration of liver enzymes and increased bilirubin (jaundice), sometimes making resection of a substantial part of the liver necessary. The cysts can grow to large sizes and invade part of a hemithorax, causing an irritative cough, hemoptysis (expectoration of fresh blood from the respiratory tract) and upper respiratory tract discomfort.

entities/edema-pulmonar/description.text: Pulmonary edema is an abnormal accumulation of fluid in the lungs, especially in the spaces between the blood capillaries and the alveoli, leading to swelling. Pulmonary edema is generally caused by heart failure. As the heart stops working properly, the pressure in the arteries going to the lung begins to rise and, as this pressure increases, fluid is forced into the alveoli. This fluid acts as a barrier that interrupts the normal movement of oxygen through the lungs, causing difficulty breathing. It can also be caused by direct injury to the lung, by a poisonous gas (common in fires producing heavy smoke) or by a severe infection. Lung damage and fluid accumulation, which is generalized in the body, are also seen in kidney failure, due to large protein losses and the consequent decrease in oncotic pressure in the blood compared with the interstitial space.

entities/edema/description.text: Edema means swelling caused by the accumulation of fluid in the body's tissues. It usually occurs in the feet, ankles and legs, but it can affect the whole body. Causes of edema include excessive salt consumption, sunburn, heart failure, kidney disease, liver problems from cirrhosis, pregnancy, problems with the lymph nodes (especially after a mastectomy), some medicines, and standing or sitting for a long time in hot weather.

entities/ego/description.text: The concept of the self (ego) is a difficult term to define because of its different meanings. Throughout history its definition has been related to other terms such as psyche, being, soul, consciousness. For psychology, the ego is the psychic agency through which the individual recognizes himself or herself as "I" and is aware of their own identity. From a spiritual perspective, ego means considering oneself distinct from others and from God due to identification with the physical body. Normally, a person with a lot of "ego" is associated with people who consider themselves very important and, consequently, are easily offended.

entities/egoismo/description.text: Psychological egoism is the theory of human nature that states that behavior is driven by self-interested motivations and denies the existence of truly altruistic behavior.

entities/elefantiasis/description.text: Elephantiasis is a syndrome characterized by the enormous enlargement of some parts of the body, especially the lower limbs and the external genital organs. It can be produced by various persistent inflammatory diseases caused by various spirochetes, treponemes and parasites. This disease is due to obstruction of the lymphatic vessels, which results in severe inflammation, and to blood parasites such as filariae (parasites that inhabit the lymphatic vessels, body cavities, heart and other places in the body depending on the species). It also causes bone malformation, which progressively deforms the body as far as the deformation allows.

entities/embarazo-extrauterino/descripti.text: The "Fallopian tube - Ovary" pair identifies an extrauterine pregnancy in one of the fallopian tubes. It must not be impacted, since a miscarriage would result. The product of conception must be pushed toward the uterus; the way to do this is to identify the polarity of the fallopian tube in question and use the magnet with that same polarity to push the embryo toward the uterus; once in the uterus, the problem is resolved and the pregnancy develops normally. As soon as the "Fallopian tube - Ovary" pair depolarizes, it indicates that the embryo has implanted in the uterus. Likewise, when the uterus becomes polarized, this also indicates that the embryo has implanted in the uterus. Traditional medicine cuts the tube and everything is discarded.

entities/embarazo/description.text: True pregnancy. It must not be impacted, as it produces miscarriages. This pair confirms that a woman is pregnant. The scan is done with the negative pole, identifying the ovary; the magnet is then removed and the positive pole is placed on the uterus. The 2 magnets must not be placed at the same time. Ectopic pregnancy (outside the uterus --> in the tubes) is identified by the Tube - Ovary pair, which must not be impacted either. The uterus becomes polarized with the baby's sex: male --> positive, female-->negative.

entities/encefalitis/description.text: Encephalitis is irritation and swelling (inflammation) of the brain, almost always due to infections. Encephalitis is an uncommon disease. It occurs most often in the first year of life and decreases with age. The most frequent cause of encephalitis is a viral infection, and many types of virus can provoke it. Encephalitis caused by herpes simplex virus is the main cause of the most severe cases at all ages, including newborns. The virus causes inflammation of the brain tissue. This tissue swells (cerebral edema), which can destroy neurons and cause bleeding in the brain (intracerebral hemorrhage) and brain damage. Some patients may have symptoms of a cold or a stomach infection before the symptoms of encephalitis begin. When a case of encephalitis is not very severe, the symptoms may be very similar to those of other illnesses, including: fever that is not very high, headache, low energy and loss of appetite. The Temporal - Frontal bone pair is related to the inflammatory lesions caused by encephalitis.

entities/encefalotopia-espongiforme/desc.text: Mad cow disease and the disease that consumption of its meat produces in people belong to the group of diseases called transmissible spongiform encephalopathies (TSE). These pathologies are produced by the action of a prion protein whose shape is altered. The first symptoms are depression, delusions and hallucinations. Then comes ataxia (stiffness of the limbs and loss of movement control). The disease degenerates into dementia and the victims usually die one year later.

entities/endocarditis/description.text: Endocarditis is a disease that occurs as a result of inflammation of the endocardium, that is, an inflammatory process localized in the inner lining of the heart's chambers and valves (whether native or prosthetic). It is characterized by colonization or invasion of the heart valves with the formation of vegetations composed of platelets, fibrin, microcolonies of microorganisms and, occasionally, inflammatory cells. Other structures that can be affected are the interventricular septum, the chordae tendineae, the mural endocardium and even intracardiac implants. There are several ways of classifying endocarditis; the simplest is based on etiology, which can be infectious or noninfectious, depending on whether or not the cause of the inflammation is a microbe. This disease is different from inflammation of the heart muscle, called myocarditis, and from inflammation of the outer lining of the heart, called pericarditis. These last two conditions are usually caused not by microbes but by autoimmunity or viruses, and in many cases the cause is unknown.

entities/endolimax-nana/description.text: Endolimax nana is a commensal parasite found exclusively in the human intestine; that is, it lives at the expense of humans but does not harm them. Although it does not cause disease in humans, its pathogenicity for humans is nevertheless a debated subject, since clinical cases of chronic diarrhea, enterocolitis or urticaria associated with its presence are reported periodically. Endolimax nana, as the species name would seem to suggest, is a dwarf amoeba, rarely measuring more than 10 μm. Human infections are due to the ingestion of viable cysts; infection by this amoeba indicates contamination of food and drink or poor personal hygiene. It has a cosmopolitan distribution and, like Entamoeba coli, it is prevalent in most populations, being higher in warm, humid climates and in areas where personal hygiene is deficient.

entities/endometriosis/description.text: Endometriosis consists of the appearance and growth of endometrial tissue outside the uterus, in the pelvic cavity, on the ovaries, behind the uterus, on the uterine ligaments, in the urinary bladder or in the intestine. It produces urination disorders, intestinal obstruction, digestive bleeding.

entities/enfermedad-del-sueno/descriptio.text: Sleeping sickness is an infection with germs transmitted by certain flies that causes inflammation of the brain. When an infected fly bites, the infection spreads through the blood. Some of the symptoms of sleeping sickness are the following: anxiety, lethargy during the day, fever, headache, insomnia, mood changes, drowsiness (may be uncontrollable), sweating, swollen lymph nodes all over the body, a swollen, red and painful nodule at the site of the fly bite, weakness.

entities/enfermedad-pulmonar-intersticia.text: Interstitial lung diseases are a varied group of diffuse inflammatory disorders of the lower airways caused by inflammation and fibrosis (scarring) of the alveolar walls and thickening of the surrounding interstitium. They tend to progress toward the progressive loss of functional alveolocapillary units, causing breathing difficulty that evolves into respiratory failure. Some symptoms are the following: dry, nonproductive cough, dyspnea with decreased exercise tolerance and exhaustion, hammer-shaped or drumstick fingers (clubbing, not always present), dry crackling rales on auscultation, pulmonary hypertension.

entities/enfermedad-pulmonar-obstructiva.text: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a lung disorder characterized by the presence of airway obstruction that is generally progressive and irreversible. A higher incidence is found in people exposed to tobacco smoke, and its main symptom is a decrease in respiratory capacity that advances slowly over the years and causes considerable deterioration in the quality of life of those affected, and may lead to premature death. Between 20 % and 25 % of smokers develop the disease, but the causes of the predisposition to develop it are unknown, although it may be a multifactorial component that includes environmental elements such as smoking, air pollution, dust and chemicals in the workplace, and infections.

entities/enfisema-pulmonar/description.text: Pulmonary emphysema is defined in pathological terms as permanent enlargement of the air spaces distal to the terminal bronchioles, with destruction of the alveolar wall, with or without overt fibrosis. It is a chronic disease that, together with chronic bronchitis, is included in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). In the lungs there is thought to be a balance between the synthesis and degradation of elastin, a component of the alveolar wall that is essential for maintaining the elastic properties of the lung. Emphysema appears when an imbalance occurs, either because elastolytic capacity increases or because anti-elastolytic activity decreases. Tobacco smoke and other pollutants are believed to trigger the release of chemicals (mainly oxidants) that damage the walls of the alveoli. The damage worsens over time. People with this disease have pulmonary alveoli that are able to fill with fresh air but cannot easily expel it, which affects the supply of oxygen to the body. A substance that exists naturally in the lungs, called alpha-1-antitrypsin (AAT), can protect against this damage. AAT, produced by hepatocytes, is the most abundant protease inhibitor in human serum and the lung's main defense against elastase. People with alpha-1-antitrypsin deficiency are at greater risk of developing this disease.

entities/entamoeba-histolytica/contagion.text: Mode of transmission: fecal-oral route or sexual/anal contact. Infection occurs through contamination of water, vegetables, fruit or other raw foods that are poorly washed or undercooked with infectious cysts from contaminated feces.

entities/entamoeba-histolytica/descripti.text: Entamoeba histolytica is very aggressive. It infiltrates the brain. It causes amoebiasis, including amoebic colitis and liver abscess. The lesions it produces can be intestinal or extraintestinal. Intestinal pathology occurs mainly in any part of the colon, particularly the cecum, sigmoid colon and rectum. Extraintestinal lesions include: 1) Pulmonary location: generally arising by contiguity from hepatic lesions, seen more frequently in the right lung. It is characterized by necrosis of the lung parenchyma with possible secondary bacterial infection. 2) Cerebral location: caused by hematogenous spread. It is a rather rare complication. 3) Location in the skin: causing dermal ulcers, seen more frequently in the perianal region, penile region and abdominal wall. 4) Liver abscess.

entities/enteritis-necrotica/description.text: Necrotic enteritis caused by Clostridium perfringens is frequently fatal. This disease also begins as a result of ingesting a large number of bacteria of this type in contaminated food. Deaths due to necrotic enteritis are caused by infection and necrosis of the intestines as well as by septicemia. This disease is uncommon.

entities/enteritis/description.text: Enteritis is an inflammation of the small intestine. Germs settle in the small intestine and cause inflammation and swelling. Enteritis can also be caused by an autoimmune disorder, such as Crohn's disease, by certain drugs, by radiotherapy or by celiac disease (an autoimmune reaction to gluten consumption). The inflammation may also involve the stomach (gastritis) and the large intestine (colitis).

entities/enterobacter-cloacae/descriptio.text: Enterobacter cloacae is a bacterium belonging to the genus Enterobacter, of the family Enterobacteriaceae. It is an oxidase-negative, catalase-positive Gram-negative bacillus present (as local microbiota) in the human digestive system. Cases of urinary tract infections, surgical wound infections and even bacteremia have been described. However, the most frequent are nosocomial infections in immunocompromised patients. Some conditions related to this bacterium are: perforation of the digestive tract, diarrhea, rectal bleeding, digestive problems, gas, malabsorption, colon distension and displacement to the other side of the abdomen, hemorrhoids. Bismuth helps.

entities/enterobacter-pneumoniae/descrip.text: Enterobacter is a genus of gram-negative, facultatively anaerobic bacteria of the family Enterobacteriaceae. It causes lung problems. Pneumonitis: lung inflammation limited to the interstitium. Halitosis: bad breath or unpleasant mouth odor. Otitis: inflammation of the ear and/or its tissues and parts. Laryngitis: inflammation of the larynx. Laryngitis is considered acute if it lasts a couple of days. It is considered chronic if it lasts more than two weeks.

entities/enterobius-vermicularis/contagi.text: It mainly infects children under 12 years of age, who can acquire it by eating contaminated food or by scratching the anus due to the itching produced by egg-laying in the perianal area and then putting their hands to their mouth.

entities/enterobius-vermicularis/descrip.text: Enterobius vermicularis is a small nematode parasite of humans popularly known as pinworm. It causes the intestinal disease known as oxyuriasis or piduyes, whose correct name is enterobiasis. Symptoms may include intense pain and itching around the anus, especially during nighttime rest, sleep disturbance and weight loss.

entities/enterococcus/description.text: Enterococcus is a genus of lactic acid bacteria; they are Gram-positive cocci that occur in pairs or chains. Enterococcus causes important clinical infections, including urinary tract infection, bacteremia, endocarditis, diverticulitis (inflammation of diverticula in the intestines) and meningitis. An important characteristic of this genus is its high level of antibiotic resistance. It can cause diarrhea, rectal bleeding and digestive tract problems.

entities/enterovirus/description.text: Enteroviruses are a family of viruses that cause disease in people and animals and usually affect the intestines in particular. They are contagious, so we must be careful when in contact with someone who has one. Not everyone exposed to enteroviruses will develop a disease; it all depends on their immune system. Even if they have no symptoms, they can still transmit the infection, since enteroviruses can survive inside the body for several weeks. There are many kinds of enteroviruses, most of them related to well-known diseases such as: poliomyelitis, fever syndrome, aseptic meningitis, conjunctivitis, herpangina, myopericarditis, hand-foot-and-mouth syndrome, encephalitis, among several others. Being viral, diseases caused by enteroviruses are not treated with antibiotics, and some of them are susceptible to certain antivirals. Some of their symptoms are headache, dizziness, diarrhea.

entities/envidia/description.text: Envy is that feeling or mental state in which there is pain or unhappiness at not possessing oneself what another has, whether goods, superior qualities or other kinds of things.

entities/epiglotitis/contagion.text: The main cause is a bacterium, Haemophilus influenzae, although other organisms may be involved in some cases, such as Streptococcus pneumoniae, Neisseria meningitidis and staphylococci.

entities/epiglotitis/description.text: Epiglottitis is a disease characterized by sudden inflammation of the supraglottic supporting structures, specifically the epiglottis and the arytenoid muscles. The resulting swelling of these structures leads to a life-threatening upper airway obstruction in the patient, usually children. Epiglottitis presents with sudden stridor, preceded by fever, inspiratory retractions, and characteristic salivation and drooling. In most cases, endotracheal intubation must be performed immediately by a qualified health professional.

entities/epilepsia/description.text: Epilepsy is a chronic disease characterized by one or more neurological disorders that leave the brain predisposed to generating recurrent seizures. Epilepsy can be produced by an abnormality in the neural networks of the brain and by an imbalance of the chemicals that transmit nerve signals (neurotransmitters). Epilepsy occurs when permanent changes in brain tissue cause the brain to be too excitable or agitated. The brain sends abnormal signals, which causes repetitive and unpredictable seizures. (A single seizure that does not happen again is not epilepsy.) Epilepsy may be due to a medical disorder or an injury that affects the brain, or the cause may be unknown (idiopathic). Symptoms vary from one person to another. Some people may have simple absence episodes, while others have loss of consciousness and violent shaking. The type of seizure or epileptic attack depends on the part of the brain affected and the cause of the epilepsy. Most of the time, the seizure is similar to the previous one. Some people with epilepsy have a strange sensation (such as tingling, smelling an odor that is not really there, or emotional changes) before each seizure. This is called an aura. Some medicinal plants that have shown benefits in treating epilepsy are the following: Tumba vaquero (Ipomoe stans), Valerian (Valeriana edulis ssp. procesa) and Hierba Ojo de Gallina (Galphimia glauca). On one occasion a patient with a tumor in one of her breasts came to Dr. Goiz's practice; after the treatment, and once a few minutes had passed, the tumor disappeared; however, part of the exudate went to the brain and the patient began to have seizures; when the Cerebellum-Cerebellum pair was placed, the patient stabilized.

entities/epstein-barr-virus-reservorio/c.text: Its transmission requires close personal contact, and it is transmitted through saliva, in which it remains active for several hours. For this reason, mononucleosis is also known as the "kissing disease" or "lovers' fever".

entities/epstein-barr-virus/contagion.text: Its transmission requires close personal contact, and it is transmitted through saliva, in which it remains active for several hours. For this reason, mononucleosis is also known as the "kissing disease" or "lovers' fever".

entities/epstein-barr-virus/description.text: Epstein–Barr virus is a virus of the herpesvirus family (a family that also includes herpes simplex virus and cytomegalovirus). It is the main cause of acute infectious mononucleosis, a common syndrome characterized by fever, sore throat, extreme fatigue and swollen lymph glands. Most Epstein–Barr virus infections in children or adolescents are asymptomatic and present as pharyngitis with or without tonsillitis. By contrast, in adults 75 % of cases present infectious mononucleosis. Fatigue, malaise and myalgia begin to appear 1 to 2 weeks before the fever and sore throat appear. The fever is usually not very high. Lymphadenopathy (a disorder of the lymph nodes) is seen preferentially in the cervical nodes, but many others may be affected. Some other symptoms include dizziness, irritability, mental confusion, neurological symptoms, fatigue. Psychiatric disorders, paranoia, compulsive-repulsive syndrome, schizophrenia, epilepsy.

entities/equilibrio-emocional/descriptio.text: Emotional balance is the term for the appropriate emotional responses that an individual gives toward the surrounding environment. Although the notion of appropriateness may suffer from a certain vagueness, it is important to note that imbalance is the consequence of a relationship between the subject and the environment that generates profound dissatisfaction. Emotions are psychophysiological reactions that represent modes of adaptation to certain stimuli when the individual perceives an important object, person, place, event or memory. Psychologically, emotions alter attention, raise certain behaviors of the individual in rank and activate relevant associative networks in memory.

entities/eritemas/description.text: Erythema is a dermatological medical term denoting reddening of the skin brought about by inflammation due to excess blood flow through vasodilation. Erythema is a sign of various infectious and skin diseases. In most cases, the redness disappears on its own after a short time. Erythema is normally the most visible sign of inflammation and often covers a small area, a small areola around the site where the "sensation is triggered," for example an acne papule or pustule. Erythema is a skin lesion characterized by reddening of the skin, limited or extensive, permanent or transient, due to vascular phenomena, thus producing vasodilation. It occurs, for example, with burns caused by the sun.

entities/eructos/description.text: Belching is the release through the mouth of gas from the digestive tract (mainly from the esophagus and stomach) that becomes trapped there after being swallowed while eating. It is often accompanied by a characteristic sound. Every time something is ingested, air is also swallowed along with the liquid or food. The accumulation of air in the upper part of the stomach causes it to stretch. This triggers relaxation of the muscle at the lower end of the esophagus (the tube that runs from the mouth to the stomach). This allows the air to escape upward through the esophagus and out through the mouth. Excessive or repetitive belching can be caused by unconscious swallowing of air (aerophagia). Depending on the cause, belching may last longer or be louder. Symptoms such as nausea, dyspepsia (poor digestion) and gastric acidity can be relieved by belching.

entities/escalofrio/description.text: A chill is a physiological reaction of the body to the sensation of cold, as when the body is exposed to a lower-temperature environment, and it can present with a phase of shivering together with pallor. Although not exclusively, a chill can be associated with "goose bumps" and a feeling of cold. Chills are driven by rapid relaxations and contractions of the muscles and serve as a way of generating heat when the body senses that it is cold. For this reason, they can also be a sign of the initial phase of an infectious disease, being generally associated with fever, as in the case of malaria. In the case of native populations of Siberia, it has been discovered that they have genetic adaptations to cold that help body fat produce heat directly without needing to shiver (instead of supplying energy to the muscles and brain to produce heat through shivering), through a process known as non-shivering thermogenesis.

entities/escherichia-coli-atipica/descri.text: Escherichia coli, in its natural habitat, lives in the intestines of most healthy mammals. It is the main facultative anaerobic organism of the digestive system. In healthy individuals, that is, if the bacterium does not acquire genetic elements encoding virulence factors, the bacterium acts as a commensal, forming part of the intestinal flora and thus helping in the absorption of nutrients. In humans, Escherichia coli colonizes the gastrointestinal tract of a newborn by adhering to the mucus of the large intestine within 48 hours after the first feeding. Modified or pathogenic Escherichia coli produces toxins that can cause serious diseases, intestinal and extraintestinal infections, such as infections of the excretory system and urinary tract, cystitis, urethritis, meningitis, peritonitis, mastitis, septicemia and pneumonia.

entities/esclerosis-lateral-amiotrofica/.text: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a disease of the nervous system that attacks the nerve cells (neurons) in the brain and spinal cord. These neurons transmit messages from the brain and spinal cord to the voluntary muscles, the ones you can control, such as those of the arms and legs. At first, it causes mild muscle problems. Some people notice problems walking or running, writing, or speaking. Sooner or later, the person loses strength and cannot move. When the chest muscles begin to fail, breathing becomes difficult. Using a ventilator can help, but most people with this disease die of respiratory failure. The disease usually strikes between the ages of 40 and 60 and is more common among men than women. The cause of the disease is not known.

entities/esclerosis-multiple/description.text: Multiple sclerosis is an autoimmune disease that affects the brain and spinal cord (central nervous system). Multiple sclerosis is caused by damage to the myelin sheath, the protective covering that surrounds the neurons. When this covering of the nerves is damaged, nerve impulses slow down or stop. The nerve damage is caused by inflammation, which occurs when the body's own immune cells attack the nervous system. This can occur along any area of the brain, the optic nerve or the spinal cord. It is not known exactly what causes this to happen. This disease is commonly thought to be caused by a virus or a genetic defect, or both. Environmental factors may play a role. Symptoms vary because the location and extent of each attack can be different. Episodes can last days, weeks or months. The attacks are followed by periods of reduced or absent symptoms (remissions). The nerves in any part of the brain or spinal cord can be damaged. Because of this, the symptoms of multiple sclerosis can appear in many parts of the body. The muscular symptoms are: loss of balance, muscle spasms, numbness or abnormal sensation in any area, problems moving the arms and legs, problems walking, problems with coordination and with making small movements, tremor in one or both arms or legs, weakness in one or both arms or legs. The bladder and bowel symptoms are: constipation and fecal leakage, difficulty starting urination, frequent need to urinate, intense urgency to urinate, urine leakage (incontinence). The eye symptoms are: double vision, eye discomfort, rapid and uncontrollable eye movements, loss of vision (usually affecting one eye at a time). Symptoms of numbness, tingling or pain: facial pain, painful muscle spasms, itching, tingling or burning sensation in the arms and legs. Brain and neurological symptoms: decreased attention span, decreased judgment and memory loss, difficulty reasoning and solving problems, depression or feelings of sadness, dizziness or loss of balance, hearing loss. Sexual symptoms: erection problems, problems with vaginal lubrication. Speech and swallowing symptoms: slurred speech or speech that is difficult to understand, problems chewing and swallowing. Fatigue is a common and bothersome symptom as MS progresses.

entities/esguince-de-tobillo/description.text: A sprain, twist or ligament strain is an injury of the ligaments due to distension, overstretching, torsion or tearing, accompanied by hematoma, inflammation and pain that prevents further movement of the injured part. It arises when the joint region is affected by mechanical action (the demand of a sudden movement, excessive opening or closing of the joint, unnatural movement) or by violence (fall, blow). It should not be confused with dislocation, which is a more severe injury involving a change in position of the joint and separation of its bones. Nor with a tear, which is an injury of muscle tissue. The ankle is the joint of the fibula and tibia at the place where the leg joins the bones of the foot, where a protuberance is formed.

entities/esofago-de-barrett/description.text: Barrett's esophagus is a disorder in which the lining of the esophagus is damaged by gastric acid and becomes similar to that of the stomach. When eating, food passes from the throat to the stomach through the esophagus, also called the food pipe or swallowing tube. A ring of muscle fibers at the lower end of the esophagus prevents the stomach contents from coming back up. If these muscles do not close tightly, harsh acid can leak into the esophagus, which is called reflux or gastroesophageal reflux. This can cause tissue damage over time. This syndrome generally causes no symptoms.

entities/esperma-baja-produccion/descrip.text: A sperm concentration of 20 million per ml of semen or higher is considered normal. Greater than 40 million/ml indicates increased fertility. A count of 10 million or less indicates subfertility. Total inability of the testicles to produce sperm is rare and affects very few men. Factors that can cause infertility in men are ejaculation disorders, health problems, lifestyle-related problems, environmental factors, psychological factors, stress. The biomagnetic pairs Oesophageal hiatus - Right testicle and Right testicle - Oesophageal hiatus placed simultaneously allow adequate sperm production.

entities/espina-bifida/description.text: Spina bifida is a congenital malformation in which there is incomplete closure of the neural tube at the end of the first month of embryonic life and, subsequently, incomplete closure of the last vertebrae. The main cause of spina bifida is folic acid deficiency in the mother during the months before pregnancy and in the following three months, although in 5% of cases the cause is unknown. Current research highlights that spina bifida does not have a hereditary component. It has also been shown that a person with spina bifida will not necessarily have children with the same disability. There are basically two types of spina bifida: spina bifida occulta and open or cystic spina bifida.

entities/espiroqueta/description.text: It produces false diabetes mellitus and digestive problems. Rectal irritation, bleeding, pelvic disorders. Spirochetes (Spirochaetes or Spirochaetae) are a phylum of Gram-negative bacteria that have elongated, helically coiled cells. The phylum Spirochaetes is divided into families, all included in a single order, Spirochaetales. Medically important members of this phylum are: 1) Leptospira, which causes leptospirosis or Weil's disease. 2) Borrelia burgdorferi, which causes Lyme disease. 3) Borrelia recurrentis, which causes relapsing fever. 4) Treponema pallidum, which causes syphilis. 5) Brachyspira, which causes intestinal spirochetosis.

entities/espondilitis-anquilosante-de-ca.text: Ankylosing spondylitis is a type of arthritis that primarily affects the spine or back. Spondyl refers to the spine; itis means inflammation. Ankylosing is a term that means rigid. In AS, the joints and ligaments that normally allow the spine to move and flex become inflamed. The inflammation produces pain and stiffness that usually begins in the lower back. Over time, the disease may progress to the upper spine, chest and neck. As a result, the joints and bones (vertebrae) may fuse, causing the spine to become rigid and inflexible. Other joints, such as the hips, shoulders, knees or ankles, can also become inflamed. Ankylosing spondylitis can become a chronic (long-lasting) disease. The severity of symptoms and disability varies from person to person. Early diagnosis and appropriate treatment can help control the pain and stiffness associated with AS and reduce or prevent further deformity. When children have ankylosing spondylitis, the symptoms usually begin in the hips, knees, heels or big toe and then progress to the spine.

entities/espondilitis-anquilosante/descr.text: Ankylosing spondylitis. False arthritis. It is a chronic rheumatic autoimmune disease with pain and gradual stiffening of the joints. It belongs to the group of so-called seronegative spondylopathies or spondyloarthropathies. Seronegative because the RF (rheumatoid factor) blood test result is negative, unlike rheumatoid arthritis, in which it is positive. The spondyloarthropathies include reactive arthritis, psoriatic arthritis and intestinal inflammation, including ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease. It mainly affects the spine and the ligaments, an inflammation of the skeletal musculature called enthesitis, especially in the cervical and lumbar regions and the sacroiliac joint, but it can also affect other joints of the body such as the hip, knees, shoulders and the Achilles tendon. During the course of the disease, ocular inflammation may also appear in the iris (iritis) and in the anterior uvea (uveitis). Other organs such as the kidneys and lungs may also be affected. Stiff neck.

entities/espondilosis/description.text: Spondylosis is the name given to a gradual, degenerative disc disease process that affects the intervertebral discs and the cushioning cartilaginous pads located between the vertebrae. It is sometimes also known as Degenerative Disc Disease (DDD). With aging, the body's structures lose water, density and volume and become weaker. In the intervertebral discs this process takes the form of thinning, with partial loss of their cushioning function. This causes the discs and the intervertebral joints to wear out prematurely. When the thinning of the discs reaches an advanced stage, a narrowing of the intervertebral spaces can be seen on an X-ray or other imaging study. Any level of the spine can be affected, and its clinical expression is usually pain localized in the affected area. This chronic degenerative process can come to affect the vertebral bodies and even the bone marrow. Spondylosis progresses with age and frequently develops in several intervertebral spaces. It is the most common cause of progressive compression of the spinal cord and nerve roots.
