Main cause of diabetes mellitus and appendicitis. It causes intolerance to gluten and to other foods. It can affect the gastrointestinal tract, either through the physical presence of Staphylococcus aureus or through ingestion of the staphylococcal enterotoxin secreted by the bacterium. Gastroesophageal reflux. Problems in the larynx, trachea and pleura. At present, this microorganism is the leading cause of nosocomial infections. This situation is favored by the fact that this species inhabits both the mucous membranes and the skin of humans, which allows it to enter the patient's bloodstream through surgical wounds by direct or indirect contact with healthcare personnel, with a contaminated object or even with another patient. It is serious if the Pleura – Appendix pair is associated with the Pericardium – Pericardium pair.

entities/streptococcus-agalactiae-o-stre.text: Nasopharyngeal manifestations; it affects the larynx and the upper airways. Group B streptococcus is a type of bacterium (germ) that lives in the intestine, the rectum and the vagina (in women). Most people who become ill with group B streptococcus are newborns who are exposed to the bacterium during birth. Group B streptococcus generally causes no symptoms in healthy adults. Babies who have group B streptococcus may develop the following symptoms: fever, difficulty feeding, lethargy (the baby is tired, hard to wake, floppy or inactive), and difficulty breathing (with great difficulty breathing; the baby's skin, lips or nails may turn blue). It causes meningitis in newborns and pregnancy disorders in women. Miscarriages. Disturbances at the level of the cardia. Acute rheumatic fever, tonsillitis, scarlet fever, acute glomerulonephritis and necrotizing fasciitis. Reflux, gastritis, colitis, food intolerance. Very aggressive. Barrett's esophagus (esophageal varices). Joint pain.

entities/streptococcus-c/description.text: The genus Streptococcus is a group of bacteria made up of gram-positive cocci belonging to the phylum Firmicutes and the lactic acid bacteria group. It causes skin and eye lesions, intestinal disorders, obstruction, meteorism, diarrhea, irritable colon, strangulation, diverticula, sore throat, tonsillitis, high fever.

entities/streptococcus-faecalis-o-entero.text: It is transmitted through food and wine. In hospitals. In some places grapes are trodden by foot to produce wine; if the feet are contaminated, the wine becomes an infectious agent.

Enterococcus faecalis is a commensal Gram-positive bacterium that inhabits the gastrointestinal tract of humans and other mammals. It affects the upper limbs and neck. It troubles the spleen, neck and thorax. False multiple sclerosis; it infiltrates the spinal cord and damages it, and can cause quadriplegia. It can cause endocarditis and infections of the bladder, prostate and epididymis; nervous system infections are less common.

entities/streptococcus-g/description.text: The genus Streptococcus is a group of bacteria formed by gram-positive cocci belonging to the phylum Firmicutes and the lactic acid bacteria group. It can cause cystitis (inflammation of the urinary bladder), urethritis (inflammation of the urethra), vaginitis (inflammation of the vaginal mucosa), kidney problems; in children it produces nocturia (nighttime urination) and in adults urinary incontinence. It corrects enuresis, which is the persistence of uncontrolled voiding (the process of emptying the urinary bladder when it is full of urine) beyond the age at which bladder control is achieved (4-6 years as the upper limit). Combined with streptococcus A it produces psoriasis (a chronic inflammatory skin disease that produces thickened, inflamed, scaly lesions, frequently appearing on the elbows, knees, scalp, abdomen and back). It can also cause scabies, a skin disease caused by the parasitic mite Sarcoptes scabiei, commonly called the itch mite.

entities/streptococcus-pneumoniae-o-neum.text: Pneumococcus is a Gram-positive bacterium with an oval shape and a lanceolate distal end; it is nonmotile, does not form endospores, and is an alpha-hemolytic member of the genus Streptococcus. It is an almost exclusively human pathogen that causes a large number of infections (pneumonia, sinusitis, peritonitis, etc.) and severe invasive processes (meningitis, sepsis, etc.), particularly in the elderly, children and immunosuppressed people. It is the main microorganism causing community-acquired pneumonia. Pneumococcus produces pneumonias (fulminant pneumonia). The bacterium produces an exudate (mucus) that becomes lodged at the diaphragm. When all that accumulated mucus cools, it passes into the lung and pneumonia ensues. It also produces otitis media and meningitis.

entities/streptococcus-pyogenes-o-strept.text: Direct contact with people who are ill or who carry the germ, probably through nasal or throat discharges. Casual contact rarely leads to infection. Food, especially dairy and egg products, can be contaminated by infected people and cause outbreaks of throat infection.

Group A streptococcus (GAS) is a bacterium commonly found on the skin and in the throat. It produces tonsillitis and impetigo. It also causes acute rheumatic fever, scarlet fever, acute glomerulonephritis and necrotizing fasciitis. If tonsillitis is not treated, rheumatic fever can develop, a disease that affects the joints and heart valves. It manifests with skin problems and, combined with Streptococcus G, produces psoriasis (a chronic inflammatory skin disease that produces thickened, inflamed, scaly lesions, frequently appearing on the elbows, knees, scalp, abdomen and back). Obstruction of the coronary arteries: the use of a bypass can be avoided by using biomagnetism. Fat plaques in the blood are what obstruct the coronary arteries. The cholesterol level is not important. What makes the fat plaques adhere to the coronary arteries? A pathogen: Streptococcus pyogenes (group A Streptococcus).

entities/streptococcus-salivarius/descri.text: Streptococcus salivarius is a species of spherical Gram-positive bacterium that mainly colonizes the mouth and upper respiratory area of humans a few hours after birth; therefore, additional exposure to these bacteria is harmless. They are considered an opportunistic pathogen, rarely found in the bloodstream, where it has been implicated in cases of septicemia in people with neutropenia (an acute or chronic decrease in blood granulocytes, an abnormal blood condition that can predispose the human body to infections). Symptoms may not be present; the most common are: fever above 38.5 °C, chills and malaise, weakness and fatigue, vascular ulcers (lips, gums and pharynx), cough or shortness of breath (dyspnea).

entities/surfactante/description.text: Pulmonary surfactant is a substance present in the lungs, specifically in the alveoli. It is composed of 80% phospholipids, 12% proteins and 8% other lipids. Its main function is to reduce alveolar surface tension. Surfactant has a dual function: on the one hand, it lowers the surface tension of the alveoli during expiration, preventing the alveolar collapse that would cause breathing difficulties. On the other hand, it has an immunological defense function against pathogenic bacteria and viruses, preventing these infectious agents from crossing the capillaries via the inspired air and invading the bloodstream, causing infectious disease in the lung or other organs. A deficiency in the quantity and/or quality of surfactant causes significant alterations in lung function. One example is hyaline membrane disease, which occurs in premature newborns who at birth do not yet have enough pulmonary surfactant in their alveoli, which enormously increases the work they must do with each inspiration to bring air into the lungs and may cause their death.

entities/taenia/description.text: Taenia is a genus of parasitic flatworms of the class Cestoda, commonly known as tapeworms or solitary worms. They cause two types of parasitic disease, depending on whether they are produced by the adult stage or by the larval stage. Taeniasis is the disease that occurs due to the presence of the adult forms, when they lodge in the intestine of the definitive host, and cysticercosis or coenurosis is the one produced by the larval, intermediate or juvenile forms, when they affect the intermediate hosts in their tissues or internal organs. The parasite can measure from 2 to 10 meters, and there is usually only one parasite per individual, hence its name of solitary worm. Tapeworms, which are hermaphrodites, require an intermediate host to complete their biological cycle: pig, wild boar, cattle, rabbit, goat, sheep, horse and sometimes humans. When taeniasis (the adult stage of the taenia) occurs, alterations in normal bowel function are produced, as well as inflammation of the intestinal mucosa due to the mechanical irritation of the strobila and the scolex, which also causes nervous disorders. Another of its main mechanisms of damage is its spoliative action on the nutrients digested by the host, due to the uptake of these nutrients throughout its entire body, since tapeworms feed osmotically, lacking a digestive tract. Another effect is caused by the parasite's metabolites when they are absorbed by the host, since they can induce toxic or allergic alterations, producing some general and digestive symptoms. Likewise, the action of the toxins results in neurological disorders. When cysticercosis (larval stage) occurs, the symptoms depend on the organs involved, its presence in the central nervous system being particularly important, in which case the symptoms range from constant, severe headaches and disorientation to, in severe cases, seizures, partial loss of memory and even death. When coenurosis (larval stage) occurs, the infection can cause numerous symptoms, depending on the place in the body where the larvae lodge and form cysts. These cysts are small at first but progressively increase in size until they reach a diameter of 6 cm. They very frequently lodge in the brain, causing headache, vomiting and paralysis that generally affects the right or left half of the body.

entities/talasemia/description.text: Thalassemia is a blood disorder characterized by the abnormal formation of hemoglobin, which results in deficient oxygenation and the destruction of red blood cells. There are several types, with clinical pictures ranging from hardly detectable hematological abnormalities to severe anemia and terminal illness. Hemoglobin is the substance found in red blood cells that allows them to transport oxygen throughout the body. The low hemoglobin levels and reduced number of red blood cells caused by thalassemia can cause anemia, leading to fatigue, weakness, difficulty breathing, pale appearance, jaundice, abdominal swelling, etc.

entities/taquicardia/description.text: The "Atrioventricular (AV) node region" - "Left kidney (same side)" pair corrects paroxysmal tachycardia and most other tachycardias. It corrects cardiac arrhythmias, whether the heart rate speeds up abnormally (tachycardia) or slows down (bradycardia). Tachycardia is an increase (acceleration) of the heart rate. It is the excessively rapid contraction of the ventricles. It is considered present when the heart rate is above 100 beats per minute at rest. It can be physiological (that is, non-pathological), for example, when intense physical activity is performed or when intense emotions occur (fear, anxiety, worries, nervousness about some everyday situation or any other stress-derived emotion), but it can also be associated with pathological processes such as anemia, hemorrhages, insomnia or not sleeping properly, shock, kidney failure, depression, infection of an organ, excessive nervousness and others.

entities/tejido-adiposo/description.text: For the "Navel (umbilicus) - Lumbar spine" pair, it is also suggested to place the magnets on the soles of the feet, the negative on the right side of the body and the positive on the left side. Adipose tissue, or fatty tissue, is tissue of mesenchymal origin (a type of connective tissue) formed by the association of cells that accumulate lipids in their cytoplasm: the adipocytes. On the one hand, adipose tissue performs mechanical functions: one of them is to serve as a cushion, also protecting and holding in place the internal organs as well as other, more external structures of the body; it also has metabolic functions and is responsible for generating fats for the body. There are two types of adipose tissue, white (or unilocular) adipose tissue and brown (or multilocular) fat. The cytosol and nucleus are reduced to a small area near the membrane. The rest is occupied by a large droplet of fat. Adipose tissue, which lacks ground substance, is divided into lobules by fine trabeculae of fascicular tissue. The fat in the cells is in a semiliquid state and is also composed mainly of triglycerides. It accumulates preferentially in the subcutaneous tissue, the deepest layer of the skin. Its cells, lipocytes, are specialized in forming and storing fat. This layer is called the panniculus adiposus and is an insulator against cold and heat. It acts as a cushion and also as a store of nutritional reserves. This type of tissue performs filling and cushioning functions, especially in the subcutaneous areas. It also provides structural support and an energy-reserve function. Fat varies in consistency; that is, it can be found in both liquid and solid states. In people with obesity, excess adipose tissue represents a health risk and can lead to the development of diseases.

entities/tendinitis/description.text: Tendinitis is an injury that affects the tendon of a muscle and causes its inflammation or secondary degeneration. It generally causes pain, whose location depends on the affected tendon. Some of the most frequent forms of tendinitis are supraspinatus tendinitis in the shoulder, pes anserine tendinitis in the knee and Achilles tendinitis, which affects the Achilles tendon. There is some controversy over the proper use of the term tendinitis; today the term tendinopathy or tendinosis is generally preferred to designate this type of injury, since there is often no inflammation, so the suffix -itis would not be appropriate.

entities/tenosinovitis/description.text: Tenosynovitis is inflammation of the lining of the sheath surrounding the tendon, the cord that joins muscle to bone. The synovial membrane is a lining of the protective sheath that covers the tendons. The term tenosynovitis refers to inflammation of that sheath. The wrists, hands and feet are frequently affected; however, the condition can occur in any tendon sheath. Some of the symptoms related to tenosynovitis are: difficulty moving a joint, pain when moving a joint, redness along the length of the tendon, joint swelling in the affected area, pain and tenderness around the joint, especially the wrist, ankle, foot or hand. Fever, swelling and redness may indicate the presence of an infection, especially if these symptoms were caused by a puncture or cut.

entities/testiculo-no-descendido/descrip.text: Undescended testicles occur when one or both testicles fail to descend into the scrotum before birth. In most cases, a boy's testicles descend by the time he is 9 months old. Undescended testicles are quite common in babies born prematurely.

entities/testosterona/description.text: Testosterone is a steroid sex hormone of the androgen group and is found in mammals, reptiles, birds and other vertebrates. In mammals, testosterone is produced mainly in the testicles of males and the ovaries of females, and the adrenal glands also secrete small amounts. It is the main male sex hormone and also an anabolic steroid. In men, testosterone plays a key role in the development of male reproductive tissues such as the testicles and prostate, and also in promoting secondary sexual characteristics such as, for example, increased muscle and bone mass and the growth of body hair. On average, the concentration of testosterone in the blood plasma of an adult human male is ten times greater than the plasma concentration in adult human females, but since the metabolic consumption of testosterone in men is greater, daily production is approximately 20 times greater in men.

entities/tetanos/description.text: Clostridium tetani is a spore-forming, anaerobic Gram-positive bacterium. Found in nature as spores in the soil or as a parasite in the gastrointestinal tract of animals, it causes very serious infections in humans and produces the disease tetanus: cephalic tetanus, wound tetanus and neonatal tetanus. It causes urinary tract problems, affects the nervous system and produces violent muscle contractions. It produces toxins that can lead to death. Low back pain, hypertension, edema, mental confusion, fever, catarrh.

entities/tic-nervioso/description.text: A "tic" is a problem in which a part of the body moves repeatedly, quickly, suddenly and uncontrollably. Tics can occur in any part of the body, such as the face, shoulders, hands or legs. They can be stopped voluntarily for brief periods. Sounds that are made involuntarily (such as throat clearing) are called vocal tics. Most tics are mild and barely noticeable. However, in some cases they are frequent and severe and can affect many areas of the person's life. The most common tic is called "transient tic disorder"; these go away on their own. Some can be worsened by anxiety, tiredness and some medications. Some tics never go away. Tics that last for more than a year are called "chronic tics."

entities/tifo-exantematico/description.text: Epidemic exanthematous typhus, or green louse disease, is a form of typhus, so called because the disease often causes epidemics after wars and natural disasters. The causative agent is the bacterium Rickettsia prowazecki, transmitted by the human body louse. Infected lice migrate to a new host by direct contact. The microorganisms are shed in the louse's feces during the bite and are inoculated into the skin by scratching. The bacteria reach the blood and are taken up by endothelial cells, where they multiply, causing vasculitis (inflammation of the blood vessels) and thrombosis (formation of clots inside a blood vessel). Some of the symptoms are the following: irritability, nervousness, fever, migraine, mental confusion. It tests positive on febrile agglutination tests (for diseases that cause fever).

entities/tinnitus/contagion.text: They can be caused by a large number of causes, generally traumatic, or be the result of a symptom of blocked ears or of Ménière's disease. They can also be caused by stressful situations from studies, work, the family, economic or social environment, or exposure to noise.

entities/tinnitus/description.text: Tinnitus or acouphenes, which consists of a perceptual phenomenon in which knocking or sounds are perceived in the ear that do not come from any external source. They generally consist of whistling, roaring, buzzing, whispering, blowing, hissing or ringing, and sometimes become so loud that the patient is unable to hear a normal conversation.

entities/tos-cronica/description.text: Cough is the most common symptom for which medical services are consulted. Coughing is a complex reflex mechanism that makes it possible to clear the airway of secretions or particles, as well as to prevent the aspiration of foreign bodies, by means of violent expiration. Under normal circumstances it has a protective effect on the airways and lungs, but under other conditions it can become excessive and useless, turning into a potentially harmful factor. It is produced by sudden and sometimes repetitive spasmodic contraction of the chest cavity, resulting in a violent release of air from the lungs, which produces a characteristic sound. According to its components, cough can be dry: it expels only air; productive: it expels air accompanied by sputum (secretion or phlegm produced in the lungs, bronchi, trachea, larynx, pharynx); emetic: it produces vomiting (with food, bile, etc.). According to its duration, cough can be acute: less than 3 weeks, subacute: 3 to 8 weeks, and chronic: more than 8 weeks.

entities/tos-ferina/description.text: Bordetella pertussis is a gram-negative, strictly aerobic, non-spore-forming, fimbriated, encapsulated coccobacillus of the genus Bordetella. Bordetella pertussis is the agent responsible for whooping cough. Unlike Bordetella bronchiseptica, Bordetella pertussis is non-motile. Humans are the only hosts of Bordetella pertussis. The bacteria lodge in the respiratory system, attaching first to the ciliated epithelium of the respiratory tract and then to the pulmonary alveoli, causing necrosis. Whooping cough (pertussis) is a highly contagious acute infectious disease of the upper respiratory tract caused by the gram-negative bacterium Bordetella pertussis. It is characterized by tracheobronchial inflammation and typical bouts of violent, spasmodic coughing with a sensation of suffocation that end with a shrill noise during inspiration. It is a serious disease that can cause permanent disability in infants and even death. Chronic cough. It causes problems in the digestive tract, diarrhea, flatulence. In women it causes vaginal discharge.

entities/toxina/description.text: Toxins in the kidney. A toxin is a poisonous substance produced by living cells of animals, plants, bacteria or other biological organisms. To emphasize its organic origin, the term biotoxin is sometimes also used. Toxins may be small molecules, peptides or proteins capable of causing disease when they come into contact with, or are absorbed by, body tissues, interacting with biological macromolecules such as enzymes or cell receptors. Toxins vary enormously in their severity, ranging from a brief, mild effect (as in the case of a bee sting) to almost immediately fatal (as with botulinum toxin).

entities/toxocara/description.text: Toxocara is a genus of ascaridid nematodes containing several species of parasitic worms, typical of canids and felids, which only secondarily affect humans. They are cylindrical worms with pointed ends, with 3 lips around the mouth and a light pink, pearly color. Adult females measure about 15 cm, while males are almost half that. They affect humans only when there is contact with the larvae in high concentrations. It produces tertian fever (returning every third day), vomiting, laryngeal obstruction, diarrhea, skin and hair problems.

entities/toxoplasma-gondii/description.text: Toxoplasma gondii is a species of parasitic protozoan that causes toxoplasmosis, a disease that is generally mild but can become complicated to the point of being fatal. Very harmful during pregnancy; depending on the age of the fetus it can cause intrauterine death (1st trimester), malformations (2nd trimester), central nervous system involvement, hydrocephalus, cerebral calcifications, hepatosplenomegaly, jaundice, pneumonitis, myocarditis (3rd trimester). More than 80% of infections are asymptomatic and, when symptoms and signs do occur, they are usually short-lived. It can destroy structures of the ear. In children it can cause encephalomyelitis and in adults it can cause visual disturbances.

entities/tracoma/description.text: Trachoma is an inflammation of the conjunctiva caused by the bacterium Chlamydia trachomatis, which is contagious and is transmitted by direct contact with the infected person or by certain flies that feed on the secretions of infected people. It is the main cause of infectious blindness. Worldwide, this disease causes severe visual disabilities.

entities/trastorno-en-niveles-de-albumin.text: Albumin is a protein found in large proportion in blood plasma; it is the main protein of the blood and one of the most abundant in humans. It is synthesized in the liver. The normal concentration in human blood ranges between 3.5 and 5.0 grams per deciliter, and it accounts for 54.31 % of plasma protein. The rest of the proteins present in plasma are collectively called globulins. Albumin is essential for maintaining oncotic pressure, which is necessary for the correct distribution of body fluids between the intravascular compartment and the extravascular compartment, located between the tissues. Albumin has a negative electrical charge. The basement membrane of the renal glomerulus is also negatively charged, which prevents glomerular filtration of albumin into the urine. In nephrotic syndrome this property is diminished, and a large amount of albumin is lost in the urine. Because small animals, such as rats, live with low blood pressure, they need a lower osmotic pressure and also need a low amount of albumin to maintain fluid distribution.

entities/trastorno-en-niveles-de-creatin.text: Creatinine is an organic compound generated from the breakdown of creatine (a nutrient useful for the muscles). It is a waste product of normal muscle metabolism that the body usually produces at a very constant rate (depending on muscle mass) and that the kidneys normally filter, excreting it in the urine. Measuring creatinine is the simplest way to monitor proper kidney function.

entities/trastorno-en-niveles-de-urea/de.text: Urea is a crystalline, colorless chemical compound with the formula CO(NH2)2. It is found abundantly in urine and fecal matter. It is the main end product of protein metabolism in humans and other mammals. Human urine contains about 20 g per liter; an adult eliminates 25 to 39 g daily. In smaller amounts, it is present in the blood, liver, lymph and serous fluids. It is also found in the heart, lungs, bones and reproductive organs, as well as semen. Urea is formed mainly in the liver as an end product of metabolism. Urea nitrogen, which makes up 80 % of the nitrogen in urine, comes from the breakdown of various nitrogen-containing compounds, above all the amino acids of dietary proteins. In mammals, urea is formed in a metabolic cycle called the urea cycle. Because of its dipole moment, urea is soluble in water and alcohol, and slightly soluble in ether.

entities/trastorno-obsesivo-compulsivo/d.text: Obsessive–compulsive disorder (OCD) is an anxiety disorder characterized by intrusive, recurrent and persistent thoughts that produce restlessness, apprehension, fear or worry, and by repetitive behaviors called compulsions, aimed at reducing the associated anxiety. OCD symptoms can appear at any age and can produce significant disability. Various scientific studies show that patients with OCD have a very low quality of life, since this condition can be mentally and physically exhausting and can in itself be a cause of temporary or permanent work disability. Common obsessions include fear of contamination, fear that the person or others are in danger, a need to maintain order and exactness, and excessive doubts. The most common compulsions performed as a ritualistic response to these obsessions include handwashing, counting, hoarding and arranging things. It is characteristic for the person with OCD to be reluctant to reveal their symptoms to others, so it is common for them to seek help many years after the onset of the problem, as is the presence of concurrent depression. The specific cause of its onset is not known exactly, but a combination of biological factors (family history of OCD) and social factors (such as overprotective and controlling parents) may explain the alterations that have been found. Most people with OCD had excessively controlling and strict parents who never reinforced their self-esteem and who, from childhood, contributed to increasing their anxiety, insecurity and lack of self-esteem, which in the end will cause negative thoughts and worries to appear in the child and, by adolescence and adulthood, obsessions and compulsions.

entities/trastorno-por-deficit-de-atenci.text: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, or ADHD, is a chronic neuropsychiatric developmental disorder frequently diagnosed in childhood that may persist into adulthood. It is characterized by inattention (moderate to severe distractibility, short attention spans), hyperactivity (motor restlessness) and impulsive behavior (emotional instability and impulsive conduct), which produce problems in multiple areas of functioning, hindering the social, emotional and cognitive development of the person who has it. It is usually accompanied by high rates of psychiatric comorbidity. It can be associated with oppositional defiant disorder and other behavioral disorders, as well as with mood disorders, anxiety disorder, personality disorder, autism spectrum disorders or drug dependence. Symptoms usually worsen in situations that demand sustained attention or mental effort or that lack intrinsic appeal or novelty (e.g., listening to the teacher in class, doing homework, listening to or reading long texts that are not to one's liking, or working on monotonous or repetitive tasks).

entities/trastornos-bucales/description.text: The mouth is one of the most important parts of the body. Any problem affecting the mouth can make it difficult to eat, drink or even smile. Common mouth problems include: cold sores, which are painful sores on the lips and around the mouth caused by a virus; mouth ulcers; oral candidiasis, which is a Candida infection that causes whitish patches in the mouth; leukoplakia, which is characterized by the appearance of white patches formed by excess cell growth on the mucosa of the cheeks, gums or tongue (common in smokers); dry mouth, characterized by a lack of sufficient saliva; gum or tooth problems; bad breath.

entities/trastornos-cutaneos/description.text: A skin disorder is any disorder of the skin; the skin can be affected by a wide variety of disorders, from physical wounds to chemical damage. It is susceptible to infection by viruses, bacteria, fungi and protozoa, and can become infested by mites and other parasites. The skin can also develop benign and cancerous tumors, and it can be affected by an inadequate blood supply. Its own glands, blood vessels and nerves can undergo alterations, and the skin also reacts in various ways to allergy. Skin rashes and discoloration can reflect various general disorders of the body. The skin is the largest organ of the body; it covers and protects the body. Some of the functions of the skin are the following: it keeps body fluids inside the body, preventing dehydration; it protects against bacteria and viruses that can cause infections; it helps perceive the outside world, whether it is cold or hot, wet or dry; it regulates body temperature; it makes vitamin D when exposed to sunlight. Anything that irritates, clogs or inflames the skin can cause symptoms such as redness, swelling, burning and itching. Allergy, irritants, one's genetic makeup and certain diseases and immune-system problems can cause rashes, hives (urticaria) and other skin problems. Many skin problems, such as acne, also affect its appearance.

entities/trastornos-de-piso-pelvico/desc.text: The pelvic floor supports the uterus, bladder and rectum; over time it can stretch, weaken and become excessively tense, causing loss of support for the organs it previously held up, resulting in pain, bladder or bowel problems and other symptoms such as urinary urgency. Among the factors that can contribute to this problem are motherhood, obesity, menopause, stress and age. 50 percent of women over 50 years of age present weakening and some of its consequences.

entities/trastornos-de-vejiga/descriptio.text: The bladder is a hollow organ in the lower abdomen where urine is stored. Many conditions can affect bladder function. Among the most common are the following: cystitis, which is an inflammation of the bladder, generally caused by an infection; urinary incontinence, which is the loss of bladder control; overactive bladder, a condition that causes the bladder to release urine when it should not; interstitial cystitis, a chronic problem that causes bladder pain and urinary urgency; bladder cancer.

entities/trastornos-de-vision/descriptio.text: There are many types of eye problems and visual disturbances, such as: halos, blurred vision (loss of visual acuity and inability to see small details), blind spots or scotomas (dark "holes" in the visual field in which nothing can be seen). Vision loss and blindness are the most serious visual problems.

entities/trastornos-del-lenguaje/descrip.text: Language alterations, anomalies, disturbances or disorders hinder linguistic communication in a more or less persistent way, affecting not only linguistic aspects (phonological, syntactic or semantic, both at the level of comprehension and decoding and of expression or production-encoding) but also intellectual and personality aspects, interfering with the relationships and the school, social and family performance of the affected individuals.

entities/trastornos-del-sueno/descriptio.text: Sleep disorders or sleep disturbances (also known as sleep diseases or even sleeping disorders) are a broad group of conditions that affect the normal course of the sleep-wake cycle. Some sleep disorders can be very serious and interfere with the individual's physical, mental and emotional functioning. Some of the most frequent disorders are described below. Sleep apnea: when the person has one or more pauses in breathing or has shallow breathing during sleep. Enuresis: when the person wets the bed during sleep; it generally happens to children. Insomnia: insufficient, restless, poor-quality or nonrestorative sleep. Restless legs syndrome: a disorder in which one wants or needs to move the legs to interrupt uncomfortable sensations. Night terrors: a disorder characterized by the person's abrupt, terrified awakening. Sleepwalking: when people walk or carry out another activity while still asleep. Narcolepsy: when the person is very sleepy throughout the day even though they slept their full hours the night before.

entities/trastornos-dentales/description.text: Teeth are made of a hard material similar to bone. Inside the teeth there are nerves and blood vessels. Teeth are necessary for many activities such as eating, speaking and even smiling. Dental problems include caries, infections and trauma. The most common symptom of a dental problem is toothache. Others include wear or loss of teeth. Fortunately, many dental disorders can be prevented through care and cleaning of the teeth.

entities/trastornos-digestivos/descripti.text: Digestive disorders or problems are all those complaints suffered in digestion, both in the process and in elimination. Some examples are slow, heavy digestion, cramps, acid reflux, constipation, irritable bowel syndrome, gas, etc. In some cases, such as Crohn's disease or celiac disease, digestive disorders can be chronic and autoimmune in type. Although most are acute, it is true that many can become chronic if certain aspects such as stress and diet are not taken care of. These would be the so-called functional digestive disorders. There are a great number of digestive problems, and each has specific symptoms, although there are a few that are common to most: a feeling of bloating in the stomach, especially during digestion; difficulty passing stools, which may be painful; disturbances in the regularity of bowel movements; weight loss for no apparent reason; nausea or vomiting; stomach pain; diarrhea; reflux. Digestive disorders have various causes depending on whether they are autoimmune, functional or of another type. Autoimmune digestive problems are due to some deficiency of the immune system that causes it to attack and react to a harmless element, even one that is necessary for it, as if it were an infectious agent. Functional digestive problems are caused by alterations in the functioning of the digestive processes and occur without any structural lesion or damage. The great majority of these alterations are produced by lifestyle habits such as stress and poor diet.

entities/trastornos-en-coagulacion/descr.text: Coagulation is the process by which blood loses its fluidity, turning into a gel to form a clot. This process potentially results in hemostasis, that is, the cessation of blood loss from a damaged vessel, followed by its repair. The coagulation mechanism involves platelet activation, adhesion and aggregation, together with the deposition and maturation of fibrin. Coagulation disorders are disease states that can cause spontaneous bleeding, bruising or obstructive clotting (thrombosis). Coagulation begins almost instantly after a wound damages the endothelium of a blood vessel. Exposure of the blood to the space beneath the endothelium initiates two processes: changes in the platelets, and exposure of subendothelial tissue factor to plasma factor VII, which ultimately leads to the formation of fibrin. Platelets immediately form a plug at the site of injury; this process is called primary hemostasis. Secondary hemostasis occurs simultaneously; the protein coagulation factors beyond factor VII respond in a complex cascade of enzymatic reactions to form fibrin strands, which strengthen the platelet plug.

entities/trastornos-en-la-piel/descripti.text: The skin is the largest organ of the body. It has many important functions, such as regulating body temperature, maintaining fluid and electrolyte balance and perceiving painful or pleasant stimuli. The skin retains the body's chemicals and nutrients, while preventing the penetration of dangerous substances into the body, and acts as a shield that protects it from the ultraviolet rays emitted by the sun. Many of the problems that occur in the skin are limited to it. However, in some cases, the skin reveals a disorder that affects the whole body. Some of the skin diseases are the following: skin cancer, atopic dermatitis, alopecia areata, acne, scabies, psoriasis, warts, rosacea.

entities/trastornos-ginecologicos/descri.text: Gynecological disorders affect the female reproductive system. The most frequent symptoms of gynecological disorders are pelvic pain, vaginal itching, vaginal discharge, abnormal vaginal bleeding, and breast pain and lumps. The significance of these symptoms often depends on the woman's age, since they may be related to the hormonal changes that occur with age.

entities/trastornos-neurologicos/descrip.text: A neurological disease or neurological disorder is any disorder of the body's nervous system. Structural, biochemical or electrical abnormalities in the brain, spinal cord or other nerves can give rise to a range of symptoms. Examples of symptoms include paralysis, muscle weakness, lack of coordination, loss of sensation, seizures, confusion, pain and altered levels of consciousness. There are many recognized neurological disorders, some relatively common, but others rarer. The brain, the spinal cord and the nerves make up the nervous system. Together they control all the functions of the body. When something goes wrong in one part of the nervous system, you may have difficulty moving, speaking, swallowing, breathing or learning. There may also be problems with memory, the senses or mood.

entities/trastornos-psiquiatricos/descri.text: Psychiatric disorders are psychological patterns or abnormalities that may be reflected in behavior, that are generally associated with distress or disability, and that are not considered part of the normal development of a person's psyche. Mental disorders are generally defined by a combination of how a person feels, acts, thinks or perceives their surroundings. Some commonly known categories are specific phobias, generalized anxiety disorder, social anxiety disorder, panic disorder, agoraphobia, obsessive–compulsive disorder and post-traumatic stress disorder. A mood disorder involves unusually intense and sustained sadness, melancholy or despair, which is known as major depression. Patterns of belief, use of language and perception of reality can become disordered. Psychotic disorders in this area include schizophrenia and delusional disorder. Eating disorders involve disproportionate preoccupation with food and weight. These include anorexia nervosa and bulimia nervosa. People who are abnormally unable to resist certain impulses harmful to themselves or others may be classified as having an impulse-control disorder, including various types of tic disorders, kleptomania or pyromania. Behavioral addictions, such as gambling addiction, may be classified as a disorder.

entities/trastornos-pulmonares/descripti.text: Lung disorders are any problem in the lungs that prevents them from working properly. There are three main types of lung disease: 1) Airway diseases: these diseases affect the tubes (airways or respiratory passages) that carry oxygen and other gases into and out of the lungs. They usually cause a narrowing or obstruction of the airways. They include asthma, COPD and bronchiectasis. People with airway diseases often say they feel as if they were "trying to breathe out through a straw" (narrowing of the airways). 2) Lung tissue diseases: these affect the structure of the lung tissue. Scarring or inflammation of the tissue prevents the lungs from expanding fully (restrictive lung disease). This makes it harder for the lungs to take in oxygen and release carbon dioxide. People with this type of lung disorder often say they feel as if they were "wearing a sweater or vest that is too tight". As a result, they are unable to take a deep breath. Pulmonary fibrosis and sarcoidosis are examples of lung tissue diseases. 3) Pulmonary circulation diseases: these affect the blood vessels in the lungs. They are caused by clotting, scarring or inflammation of those vessels. They affect the ability of the lungs to take in oxygen and release carbon dioxide. They can also affect cardiac activity. An example of this type of disease is pulmonary hypertension. Many lung diseases involve a combination of these three types. The most common lung diseases include: asthma, partial or total collapse of the lung (pneumothorax or atelectasis), swelling and inflammation of the main passages (bronchial tubes) that carry air to the lungs (bronchitis), COPD (chronic obstructive pulmonary disease), lung cancer, lung infection (pneumonia), abnormal accumulation of fluid in the lungs (pulmonary edema), blocked pulmonary artery (pulmonary embolus).

entities/trastornos-renales/description.text: The symptoms caused by disorders of the kidney and urinary tract vary according to each type of disorder and the part of the system affected. Fever and a feeling of generalized malaise are frequent symptoms. Some conditions related to kidney and urinary tract disorders are: bladder infection (cystitis), bacterial infection of the kidney (pyelonephritis), kidney cancer, frequent urination without an increase in urine volume, pain on urination (dysuria), compulsive need to urinate (urgency), frequent nighttime urination (nocturia), bedwetting (enuresis), obstruction of the urethra, difficulty starting urination, a weak and irregular urine stream, enlarged prostate, narrowing (stricture) of the urethra, uncontrolled loss of urine (incontinence), presence of air in the urine, passing of large or small amounts of urine, dilute (colorless) urine, concentrated (dark yellow) urine, blood in the urine (hematuria), kidney pain, kidney stones.

entities/trastornos-urogenitales/descrip.text: Disorders of the urogenital organs. The urogenital system comprises a series of organs that, having a common embryological origin, differentiate into the urinary system and the genital system, with different functions but sharing close anatomical relationships. The urinary system consists of a group of organs and ducts that filter metabolic waste products from the blood and eliminate them to the exterior. The reproductive system is formed by the gonad and a series of ducts that transport the gametes, in addition to the copulatory organs. The anatomical overlap of the two systems is especially evident in men, where the urinary and genital organs use one structure, the urethra, as the route for emptying their products. In women, this convergence occurs at the level of the vaginal vestibule.

entities/tratamiento-prolongado-con-cort.text: Corticosteroids, or corticoids, are a variety of hormones of the steroid group (produced by the cortex of the adrenal glands) and their derivatives. The effects of corticosteroids can be divided into glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid. Corticosteroids are involved in a variety of physiological mechanisms, including those that regulate inflammation, the immune system, carbohydrate metabolism, protein catabolism and plasma electrolyte levels and, finally, those that characterize the stress response. These substances can be synthesized artificially and have therapeutic applications, being used mainly for their anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive properties and their effects on metabolism. Cortisone is a steroid (lipid) hormone. Chemically it is a corticosteroid very similar to corticosterone. It is used to treat a wide variety of ailments and can be administered intravenously, orally, intra-arterially or cutaneously. Cortisone suppresses the immune system (immunosuppressive), thereby reducing the inflammatory response and neutralizing pain and swelling at the damaged site. However, its influences on the immune system can lead to various side effects, particularly when cortisone is used over a long period of time. Some of its effects are: hyperglycemia, insulin resistance, diabetes mellitus, osteoporosis, anxiety, depression, gastritis, colitis, hypertension, stroke, erectile dysfunction, hypogonadism, hypothyroidism, perforating digestive lesions, thromboembolic events, shock, general swelling, amenorrhea and retinopathy, among other problems; the teeth turn yellow.

entities/traumatismo-craneoencefalico/de.text: Traumatic brain injury, craniocerebral trauma or encephalocranial embolism is the alteration in neurological function or other evidence of brain pathology due to trauma that causes physical damage to the brain. It represents a serious health problem and is the most common cause of death and disability in young people, not counting the major related economic repercussions. It can also be defined as the direct injury of the cranial, encephalic or meningeal structures that occurs as a consequence of an external mechanical agent and that can cause functional deterioration of the cranial contents.

entities/traumatismos/description.text: Trauma is a situation in which the body sustains physical damage. In medicine, a trauma patient is someone who has suffered serious, life-threatening injuries that can result in secondary complications such as shock, respiratory arrest and/or cardiac arrest.

entities/treponema-bucalis-o-treponema-d.text: Treponema denticola or bucalis is a gram-negative, anaerobic, motile and highly proteolytic spirochete bacterium. It remains in a complex and diverse microbial community within the oral cavity and is highly specialized to survive in this environment. It is associated with the incidence and severity of human periodontal disease. Having high levels of Treponema denticola in the mouth is considered one of the main etiological agents of periodontitis.

entities/treponema-pallidum/description.text: Treponema pallidum is a species of the genus Treponema, made up of between eight and twenty coiled spirals, which give it a rotational, corkscrew-like movement. It measures 5 to 20 microns in length and 0.5 in diameter. It is a highly contagious gram-negative spirochete. It causes several human diseases, mainly syphilis. Its basic structure consists of an axial filament enclosed in a helical cylinder of cytoplasm. The filament is morphologically similar to the bacterial flagellum and gives it motility. Treponema pallidum can survive in a human host for several decades. During the first stage of the disease, painless papules appear at the site of inoculation (the mouth, penis, vagina or anus) and rapidly ulcerate, becoming a circular or oval sore with a reddish border, resembling an open wound; this is called a chancre. The second stage may appear half a year after the chancre disappears and lasts three to six months, causing painless pinkish welts called "syphilitic clavi" on the palms of the hands and soles of the feet (which can sometimes appear at other sites such as the chest, face or back), fever, sore throat and joint pain, weight loss, hair loss, headaches and lack of appetite. In the third phase (also called the final phase), between one and twenty years after the onset of infection, syphilis reawakens to attack the nervous system or some organ directly. The most serious problems occur in this phase, and it can even cause death. Some of the problems are: eye disorders, heart disease, brain lesions, spinal cord lesions, loss of limb coordination, syphilitic or luetic aneurysm, syphilitic gumma or syphiloma, etc. Treated in time, the disease leaves no sequelae. If it is not treated in time, it can cause: skin ulcerations, circulatory problems, blindness, paralysis, dementia, neurological disorders and death.

entities/trichinella-spiralis/descriptio.text: Trichinella (pronounced "trick-in-ella") is the genus of parasitic worms of the phylum Nematoda that causes trichinellosis, also incorrectly known as trichinosis, since members of this genus are often called trichinae. The adult parasite is located in the small intestine of mammals, birds or reptiles, depending on its species, but the larvae they produce spread through the bloodstream and parasitize the skeletal musculature. It causes gastrointestinal symptoms (diarrhea), muscle and joint pain. Both local manifestations (myalgias, tetany) and systemic ones (periorbital edema, hemorrhages under the nails). It can cause cardiac, pulmonary or cerebral complications.

entities/trichinella/description.text: Trichinella (pronounced "trick-in-ella") is the genus of parasitic worms of the phylum Nematoda that causes trichinellosis, also incorrectly known as trichinosis, since members of this genus are often called trichinae. The adult parasite is located in the small intestine of mammals, birds or reptiles, depending on its species, but the larvae they produce spread through the bloodstream and parasitize the skeletal musculature. It causes gastrointestinal symptoms (diarrhea), muscle and joint pain. Both local manifestations (myalgias, tetany) and systemic ones (periorbital edema, hemorrhages under the nails). It can cause cardiac, pulmonary or cerebral complications.

entities/trichomonas/description.text: Vaginitis. Urethritis. Digestive disorders. Trichomonas are flagellated parasites. They have five or six flagella, of which the anterior ones are free, while the remaining one is directed backward, adhering to the edge of the cell and forming an undulating membrane. Trichomoniasis is a sexually transmitted infection characterized by infection of the urogenital tract of humans and other animals by protozoa of the species Trichomonas vaginalis. Some infected people have no symptoms. In women, symptoms include abnormal, abundant vaginal discharge that is light green or gray, frothy and with an unpleasant odor, and itching, burning or redness of the vulva and vagina. In men, symptoms include penile discharge, burning on urination and discomfort. The disease, being caused by a parasite, is transmissible during intercourse and can favor the appearance of other infections.

entities/trichophyton/description.text: Trichophyton is a genus of fungi characterized by the fact that they develop smooth-walled micro- and macroconidia. They cause infections of the skin, nails, beard and scalp. Back pain. Athlete's foot. Foot odor. Dermatophytosis, also known as ringworm or tinea, which is a fungal infection of the skin. Nail fungus. Superficial skin infections affecting the groin area, including the genitals, pubic region and perianal region. The fungi feed on keratin in nails, hair and dead skin.

entities/triquinelosis/description.text: Trichinellosis (also called trichinosis or trichiniasis) is a parasitic disease caused by a nematode of the genus Trichinella, acquired by eating meat containing larvae of the parasite. Most patients present a febrile picture accompanied by cephalalgia (headache) and asthenia (generalized feeling of tiredness, fatigue, physical and mental weakness).

entities/tristeza/description.text: Sadness can be a symptom of depression, which is characterized, among other things, by the person's general dejection, lowered self-esteem and feelings of pessimism, hopelessness and helplessness. It is an affective state caused by a decline in morale. It is the expression of emotional pain through crying, a downcast face, lack of appetite, etc. It often appears when our expectations are not met or when life circumstances are painful.

entities/tromboembolia-pulmonar/descript.text: Pulmonary thromboembolism (PTE) is a clinicopathological situation triggered by pulmonary arterial obstruction due to a thrombus (a clot inside a blood vessel) developed in situ or to other material coming from the venous system. This results in an oxygen deficit in the lungs. It is one of the main medical emergencies. It is a potentially fatal disease. More than 70% of patients with PTE have deep vein thrombosis (DVT), even though the thrombi may not be clinically detectable. On the other hand, approximately 50% of patients with DVT develop PTE, very frequently asymptomatic.

entities/trombosis-venosa-profunda/descr.text: Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) consists of the formation of a blood clot, or thrombus, in a deep vein. It is a form of venous thrombosis that usually affects the veins in the lower part of the leg and the thigh, such as the femoral vein or the popliteal vein, or the deep veins of the pelvis. Occasionally the veins of the arm are affected; if it occurs spontaneously, it is known as Paget-Schrötter disease. Unlike the superficial veins, close to the skin, the deep veins are interwoven within the muscle groups. A DVT can occur without symptoms, but in many cases the affected limb will become painful, swollen, red and warm, and the superficial veins may become distended, engorged with poorly circulating blood. The greatest complication of a DVT is that the clot could dislodge and travel to the lungs, causing a pulmonary embolism. According to Virchow's triad, venous thrombosis occurs through three mechanisms: decreased blood flow, damage to the blood vessel wall and an increased tendency of the blood to clot (hypercoagulability). Various medical conditions can lead to DVT, such as compression of the veins, physical trauma, cancer, infections, inflammatory diseases and some specific conditions, such as strokes, heart failure or nephrotic syndrome. There are several factors that can increase the risk of DVT, including surgery, hospitalization, immobilization, obesity, age, certain medications such as estrogen or erythropoietin, and the innate tendency to form clots known as thrombophilia.

entities/trypanosoma-brucei-gambiense/de.text: Trypanosoma brucei is a protist, a protozoan parasite found mainly in the blood that causes African trypanosomiasis (or sleeping sickness) in humans and animals (nagana) in Africa. The species parasitizes two hosts, an insect vector (the tsetse fly) and a mammalian host. Because of the great difference between these two hosts, the cell undergoes complex changes to facilitate its survival in the insect gut and in mammalian blood. It also has a unique and remarkable variant surface glycoprotein (VSG) coat in order to evade the host's immune system. Some of the symptoms are the following: leg pain and paresthesia, which is an abnormal sensation of the senses or of general sensitivity experienced as a feeling of pinpricks, tingling, numbness and/or deadness on the side where it manifests. It can progress to paralysis.

entities/trypanosoma-cruzi/description.text: Chagas disease is caused by Trypanosoma cruzi, a parasite related to the African trypanosome that causes African trypanosomiasis or sleeping sickness. In the heart it causes heart disease or heart failure, inflating the pericardial cavity. In the lungs it causes ventilatory insufficiency. In the pancreas it causes false diabetes. Chagas disease has two phases: acute and chronic. The first may occur without symptoms or with very mild symptoms. The symptoms may be: fever, a feeling of general indisposition (general malaise), swelling of one eye if the bite is near it, and an inflamed, reddened area at the site of the insect bite. After the acute phase, the disease goes into remission and no other symptoms appear for many years. When symptoms finally appear, they may include: constipation, digestive problems, heart failure, abdominal pain, palpitations, difficulty swallowing.

entities/tuberculosis-bovina/description.text: Mycobacterium bovis is a slow-growing, microaerophilic (survives with very low levels of oxygen) mycobacterium that causes bovine tuberculosis. It can also infect and cause tuberculosis in humans. Tuberculosis produces kidney stones and gallstones. Abscesses in the body. It is possibly the most prevalent infectious disease in the world. Although tuberculosis is predominantly a disease of the lungs, it can also affect the central nervous system, the lymphatic system, the circulatory system, the genitourinary system, the digestive system, the bones, the joints and even the skin. The classic symptoms of tuberculosis are a chronic cough with blood-tinged sputum, fever, night sweats and weight loss.

entities/tuberculosis-de-prostata/contag.text: Mycobacterium tuberculosis bacterium. Tuberculosis is spread through the air when infected people cough, sneeze or spit. A growing number of people worldwide contract tuberculosis because their immune system is compromised by immunosuppressive drugs, drug abuse or AIDS. Oral sex with an infected person.

entities/tuberculosis-de-prostata/descri.text: Tuberculosis of the prostate develops in parallel with tuberculosis of the lungs. The reason for the development of the disease in the prostate gland is particularly its anatomical structure. This organ includes a large flow of blood and lymph. The disease manifests when peculiar protuberances (tubercles) form in the area of the prostate. Over time, these mounds begin to fuse with one another, thus forming an infiltration. At this point, a kind of suppuration forms, followed by tissue necrosis. Over time, patients begin to suffer from the following symptoms: pain when emptying the bladder; difficulty urinating at night, a feeling of pressure in the groin area, pain in the upper part of the uterus and the penis, pain in the rectum. In the late stages of prostate tuberculosis in humans, the following symptoms may appear: decreased potency, pain during ejaculation, purulent discharge.

entities/tuberculosis-reservorio/contagi.text: Mycobacterium tuberculosis bacterium. Tuberculosis is spread through the air when infected people cough, sneeze or spit. A growing number of people worldwide contract tuberculosis because their immune system is compromised by immunosuppressive drugs, drug abuse or AIDS. Oral sex with an infected person.

entities/tuberculosis/contagion.text: Mycobacterium tuberculosis bacterium. Tuberculosis is spread through the air when infected people cough, sneeze or spit. A growing number of people worldwide contract tuberculosis because their immune system is compromised by immunosuppressive drugs, drug abuse or AIDS. Oral sex with an infected person.

entities/tuberculosis/description.text: Mycobacterium tuberculosis is a bacterium responsible for the largest number of tuberculosis cases in the world. Robert Koch described it for the first time, hence the heteronym (nickname) of this bacterium: "Koch's bacillus". Tuberculosis is a contagious bacterial infection that mainly involves the lungs but can spread to other organs. Tuberculosis is possibly the most prevalent infectious disease in the world. Although tuberculosis is predominantly a disease of the lungs, it can also affect the central nervous system, the lymphatic system, the circulatory system, the genitourinary system, the digestive tract, the bones, the joints and even the skin. The classic symptoms of tuberculosis are a chronic cough with blood-streaked sputum, fever, night sweats and weight loss. Infection of other organs causes a wide variety of symptoms: kidney stones and gallstones, abscesses in the body, sterility in men and women, kidney pain, edema and a sensation of cold. It can cause torticollis, in which the neck muscles (particularly the sternocleidomastoid muscle, the levator scapulae and, to a lesser extent, the scalene muscles) contract involuntarily and cause the head to tilt. Mental disorders.

entities/tumor-en-abdomen/contagion.text: 2 Viruses = Edema, Virus + Bacterium = Cyst, 2 Bacteria = Abscess, 2 Bacteria + Virus = Dysplasia or Metaplasia, 3 Bacteria + Virus = Slow neoplasia, 3 Bacteria + Virus + Fungus = Fast-growing neoplasia, 3 Bacteria + Virus + Fungus + Leprosy = Cancer, Cancer + Pseudomonas or Clostridium = Metastasis, Cancer + Parasites = Necrosis, Cancer + Chemotherapy or Radiotherapy = Complicated cancer, Cancer + Discouragement = Incurable cancer.

entities/tumor-en-abdomen/description.text: A tumor is any alteration of tissues that produces an increase in volume. It is an abnormal enlargement of a part of the body, which therefore appears swollen or distended. Tumor, together with redness (rubor), pain and heat, forms the classic tetrad of symptoms and signs of inflammation. In a restricted sense, a tumor is any mass or lump due to an increase in the number of cells that compose it. If this cell growth originates in various cells (polyclonal) we speak of hyperplasia, and if it is a cellular neoformation originating in a single cell (monoclonal) we call it neoplasia, regardless of whether it is benign or malignant according to whether or not it is able to infiltrate the surrounding tissues. When a tumor is malignant, it has the capacity for invasion or infiltration and for producing metastases at sites distant from the primary tumor, being a metastatic cancer.
